steps.prompt:
TASK

Using the supplied reference image, reconstruct this sci-fi cylindrical
mechanical module as a clean, editable SketchUp model.

The final output must be a SketchUp-native model.

IMPORTANT:

- DO NOT create or apply any materials.
- DO NOT apply colors or textures.
- Keep every face in SketchUp Default Material.
- Organize geometry into Groups/Components according to FUTURE MATERIAL ZONES.
- The groups must be ready for manual material assignment later.

The reference image is the primary visual source.

Do NOT redesign the object.
Do NOT add decorative sci-fi details that are not visible.
Do NOT make the model more complex than the reference.


==================================================
PRIMARY OBJECT CHARACTER
==================================================

The object is a long cylindrical sci-fi mechanical module.

Its main construction consists of:

- large cylindrical shell sections
- repeated circular reinforcement rings
- recessed circumferential bands
- a complex central mechanical coupling assembly
- vent-like radial ring details
- external longitudinal rods / braces
- rod mounting brackets
- end flanges
- circular bolt patterns
- small mechanical connectors
- layered cylindrical transition pieces


The model must preserve the visible longitudinal proportion
and the sequential arrangement of these parts.


==================================================
MODELING PRIORITY
==================================================

Always preserve the following order of importance:

1. Overall silhouette
2. Length-to-diameter proportion
3. Main cylindrical segmentation
4. Position of major rings
5. Central coupling assembly
6. External rods and brackets
7. Major recesses
8. Flange geometry
9. Fasteners
10. Small detail


Do NOT sacrifice the main form for micro detail.


==================================================
REFERENCE LIMITATION
==================================================

Only one perspective reference image is supplied.

Therefore:

- Do NOT invent complicated hidden geometry.
- Assume rotational or repeated construction where visually justified.
- Use the visible geometry as the main reference.
- For hidden rear surfaces, use the simplest structurally reasonable solution.
- Maintain consistent radial symmetry unless the visible reference clearly shows asymmetry.

Do NOT add random:

- pipes
- cables
- vents
- armor
- panels
- machinery
- holes
- connectors

that are not supported by the image.


==================================================
WORKFLOW
==================================================

Do NOT immediately model small details.

Use the following sequence.


STAGE 1 — BLOCKOUT

First model only:

- main longitudinal axis
- overall cylinder length
- overall cylinder diameter
- major cylindrical sections
- major circular rings
- central coupling volume
- large end flanges
- major silhouette changes


STAGE 2 — BLOCKOUT VALIDATION

Before adding detail, compare the blockout to the reference.

Verify:

- total length
- total diameter
- diameter transitions
- ring positions
- central assembly position
- end flange size
- large silhouette breaks

Correct proportion errors BEFORE continuing.


STAGE 3 — PRIMARY STRUCTURE

Add:

- secondary cylindrical sleeves
- circumferential reinforcement rings
- recessed circular channels
- central vent ring
- central mechanical housing
- main brackets
- large external rods


STAGE 4 — SECONDARY DETAIL

Add:

- rod mounting blocks
- flange bolts
- small connectors
- major grooves
- larger mechanical inserts
- visible segmented ring details


STAGE 5 — CLEANUP

After the form is accurate:

- correct face orientation
- remove overlapping faces
- close accidental holes
- remove floating geometry
- simplify hidden geometry
- organize all Groups and Components


==================================================
MAIN CYLINDER
==================================================

Construct the primary body using clean cylindrical geometry.

Do NOT model the cylinder as a dense triangulated mesh.

Use an appropriate SketchUp circular segment count.

The cylinder should appear smooth,
but remain lightweight and editable.

Maintain the longitudinal axis perfectly straight.


==================================================
CYLINDRICAL SEGMENTATION
==================================================

Preserve the major visible segmentation along the length.

The model includes several distinct cylindrical sections with:

- slightly different diameters
- raised collars
- recessed rings
- stepped transitions
- layered sleeves

These should be actual geometric differences,
not merely drawn lines.


==================================================
CENTRAL COUPLING ASSEMBLY
==================================================

The central mechanical assembly is one of the most important features.

Preserve:

- larger central radial housing
- layered concentric rings
- radial mechanical blocks
- visible flange-like structures
- central recessed interfaces
- adjacent ring transitions

The central assembly must remain
independently selectable from the main cylindrical body.


==================================================
VENT / RADIAL RING
==================================================

There is a visible ring containing repeated radial slots/fins.

Model this efficiently.

Create ONE representative fin / slot geometry
and repeat it radially using Components or repeated geometry.

Do NOT manually create every repeated element as unique geometry.

Maintain equal angular spacing.


==================================================
EXTERNAL LONGITUDINAL RODS
==================================================

The right section contains long external cylindrical rods / braces.

These are separate from the main cylinder.

Preserve:

- rod diameter
- rod spacing
- rod alignment
- attachment points
- end mounts
- intermediate support brackets

Use Components for repeated rods or identical mounting details.

Do not merge rods into the main cylinder.


==================================================
BRACKETS
==================================================

Rod-support brackets and mechanical mounts
must remain independently selectable.

Keep:

- main mounting blocks
- clamp-like forms
- connecting arms
- radial attachment geometry

Avoid unnecessary internal mechanical complexity.


==================================================
END FLANGES
==================================================

Both visible ends use circular flange-like geometry.

Preserve:

- outer flange diameter
- layered circular rings
- recessed seam
- major fastening points
- circumferential bolt arrangement where visible

Do not create excessive internal detail behind the flanges.


==================================================
BOLTS AND FASTENERS
==================================================

Large visible bolts may be modeled.

Use reusable Components.

Do NOT model:

- screw threads
- microscopic grooves
- invisible bolt shafts
- unnecessary internal fastener geometry

Only model fasteners large enough to affect the visible form.


==================================================
CLOSED GEOMETRY
==================================================

Avoid unintended open geometry.

Any recess should contain:

front opening
→ side wall
→ rear surface

unless the reference clearly indicates a real through-hole.

Do not leave infinitely deep cavities.

Major structural sections should be closed solids whenever practical.


==================================================
HIDDEN AREAS
==================================================

For geometry that cannot be seen from the supplied view:

DO NOT create detailed speculative structures.

Continue visible cylindrical,
radial or repeated construction logically.

Hidden geometry should be:

- simple
- clean
- structurally consistent
- symmetrical where appropriate


==================================================
MATERIAL RULE — CRITICAL
==================================================

DO NOT APPLY ANY MATERIALS.

DO NOT CREATE ANY MATERIALS.

DO NOT APPLY COLORS.

DO NOT APPLY TEXTURES.

DO NOT create:

- Base Color
- Normal
- Roughness
- Metallic
- AO
- Emissive
- Glass
- UV textures

ALL faces must remain:

SketchUp Default Material.


==================================================
GROUP BY FUTURE MATERIAL
==================================================

Even though no materials are applied,
organize the geometry according to likely future material assignment.

Use approximately the following structure:


SCI_FI_CYLINDER_MASTER

    01_MAIN_SHELL
        Main_Cylinder_Sections
        Large_Sleeves

    02_RING_AND_COLLAR
        Reinforcement_Rings
        Recessed_Rings
        Transition_Collars

    03_CENTRAL_MECHANICAL
        Central_Housing
        Central_Rings
        Radial_Blocks
        Central_Connectors

    04_VENT_STRUCTURE
        Vent_Ring
        Vent_Fins

    05_EXTERNAL_RODS
        Long_Rods
        Secondary_Rods

    06_BRACKETS
        Rod_Mounts
        Support_Brackets
        Clamp_Blocks

    07_END_FLANGES
        Front_Flange
        Rear_Flange

    08_HARDWARE
        Bolts
        Fasteners
        Small_Connectors

    09_RECESSED_DETAIL
        Groove_Parts
        Recess_Back_Plates


These groups represent FUTURE MATERIAL ZONES.

No actual materials should be assigned.


==================================================
IMPORTANT GROUPING RULE
==================================================

Group parts by future material / construction category,
NOT by every individual face.

Do NOT produce hundreds of tiny groups.

For example:

all identical shell sections that will use the same future material
may belong to the same parent group.

However,
mechanically distinct categories must remain selectable.


==================================================
COMPONENT RULE
==================================================

Use Components for repeated identical parts.

Examples:

- bolts
- vent fins
- repeated brackets
- repeated rods
- radial fasteners
- repeated collar elements

Do NOT remodel identical elements separately.


==================================================
LOOSE GEOMETRY
==================================================

No loose raw geometry should remain at the top level.

Everything must belong to:

- a Group
or
- a Component

The MASTER group should contain the complete object.


==================================================
BEVEL / CHAMFER
==================================================

Use controlled bevels/chamfers only where they affect the visible form.

Apply them to:

- major collars
- flange edges
- bracket edges
- large housing blocks
- transition pieces

Do not over-round the geometry.

Avoid excessive bevel segments.


==================================================
TOPOLOGY
==================================================

Prioritize clean SketchUp geometry.

Do NOT reproduce dense render topology.

Prefer:

- simple cylinders
- planar faces
- clean extrusions
- repeated Components
- radial arrays
- simple solid groups

Avoid unnecessary triangulation.


==================================================
FACE ORIENTATION
==================================================

All exterior visible faces must point outward.

Check for reversed faces.

Correct every reversed exterior surface.

Do not rely on two-sided rendering.


==================================================
DUPLICATE GEOMETRY
==================================================

Remove:

- duplicate faces
- overlapping coplanar faces
- duplicate edges
- floating geometry
- isolated edges
- unnecessary hidden copies

Avoid Z-fighting.


==================================================
INTERSECTIONS
==================================================

Check all connections between:

- main cylinders
- rings
- central housing
- rods
- brackets
- flanges
- bolts

Components may intentionally connect,
but unrelated solids must not randomly intersect.


==================================================
MODEL PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Keep the model reasonably lightweight.

Do not use excessive cylinder segmentation.

Do not over-model hidden surfaces.

Do not model microscopic details.

Repeated details must use Components wherever possible.


==================================================
AXIS
==================================================

Use the long central cylinder axis as the primary model axis.

Keep the full object perfectly aligned.

Place the entire model near the SketchUp world origin.

Choose a consistent longitudinal axis and maintain it
through the entire model.

The cylindrical centerline must remain perfectly straight.


==================================================
FINAL VALIDATION
==================================================

Before completion verify:

1. Overall length-to-diameter proportion matches the image.
2. Main cylinder remains perfectly aligned.
3. Major ring positions match the reference.
4. Central mechanical assembly is correctly positioned.
5. Rods remain parallel to the cylinder axis.
6. Brackets align correctly.
7. Flanges are centered.
8. Repeated radial parts use consistent spacing.
9. No accidental open holes.
10. No reversed exterior faces.
11. No duplicate coplanar geometry.
12. No floating geometry.
13. No unnecessary internal detail.
14. Repeated elements use Components.
15. Geometry remains editable in SketchUp.
16. All faces use SketchUp Default Material.
17. NO MATERIALS exist on modeled parts.
18. Geometry is grouped according to future material zones.
19. Future material zones remain independently selectable.
20. The model remains suitable for later export to Unreal Engine.


==================================================
FINAL RULE
==================================================

Do not reinterpret the design.

Do not add new sci-fi detail.

Do not use material or color to fake geometry.

Do not prioritize micro detail over overall form.

When hidden geometry is uncertain,
use the simplest reasonable cylindrical or symmetrical continuation.

The priority is:

SILHOUETTE
→ PROPORTION
→ CYLINDRICAL SEGMENTATION
→ CENTRAL ASSEMBLY
→ RINGS
→ RODS
→ BRACKETS
→ FLANGES
→ HARDWARE
→ SMALL DETAIL

The final SketchUp file must contain geometry only,
organized by future material groups,
with absolutely no final materials applied.

steps.prompt:
TASK:
Rebuild and refine the existing Blender bust so that it closely matches the provided classical female sculpture reference.

IMPORTANT:
The current model is only a rough incorrect blockout.
Do NOT preserve the current simplified facial structure, helmet-like hair, or mannequin appearance.

Use the provided sculpture image as the PRIMARY AND ABSOLUTE visual reference.

This is a faithful reconstruction task, NOT a redesign.

--------------------------------------------------
1. HEAD POSE AND PROPORTION
--------------------------------------------------

The head must be tilted noticeably upward.

Raise the chin and rotate the head backward approximately 15–20 degrees.

The sculpture should appear to be looking upward even though the eyes are covered.

Preserve:
- long elegant neck
- visible underside of chin
- natural jaw-to-neck transition
- classical female head proportions

Do NOT keep the head facing straight forward.

The current head is too upright and too simplified.

--------------------------------------------------
2. FACE
--------------------------------------------------

Create a fully modeled classical female face.

The face must include:
- defined nose bridge
- nostrils
- natural nose tip
- upper and lower lips
- subtle philtrum
- chin
- jaw
- cheek volume
- realistic classical sculptural facial planes

The eyes themselves do not need to be visible because they are covered by cloth.

However, the facial structure beneath the blindfold must still be anatomically correct.

Do NOT use a blank mannequin face.
Do NOT remove the nose or mouth.

The expression should remain calm, neutral, elegant, and statue-like.

--------------------------------------------------
3. BLINDFOLD
--------------------------------------------------

The element covering the eyes is NOT a helmet, visor, hair cap, or solid plate.

It is a soft fabric blindfold wrapped horizontally around the head.

Model it as actual folded cloth.

Required characteristics:
- covers both eyes completely
- passes across the bridge of the nose
- follows the curvature of the face
- several visible horizontal fabric folds
- compressed cloth around the temples
- slightly irregular natural folds
- thin cloth thickness
- sculpted classical drapery appearance

The blindfold must sit ON TOP of the facial anatomy.

Do NOT merge it into the skull.
Do NOT make it smooth like armor.

Create it as a separate Blender object:
Blindfold_Cloth

--------------------------------------------------
4. HAIR
--------------------------------------------------

Completely replace the current helmet-like hair.

The reference has sculpted classical female hair composed of large flowing locks.

Hair structure:
- central / near-central parting
- hair swept backward from the forehead
- large sculpted strand groups
- braided or twisted crown-like sections around the upper head
- voluminous hair at the rear
- long wavy hair descending behind the neck
- visible heavy lock on the sculpture's right side

Model the hair using large sculpted masses and grooves.

Do NOT create individual realistic hair strands.
Do NOT create a smooth solid helmet.

The hairstyle should look carved from stone.

Use separate logical hair objects if helpful:
Hair_Front
Hair_Crown
Hair_Back
Hair_Long_Locks

--------------------------------------------------
5. NECK AND SHOULDERS
--------------------------------------------------

The neck must be long, slender, and anatomically believable.

Add:
- sternocleidomastoid indication
- subtle throat structure
- clavicles
- shoulder transition
- upper chest

Avoid exaggerated bodybuilder anatomy.

The shoulder width and neck proportions should resemble a classical female marble bust.

--------------------------------------------------
6. CLOTHING / DRAPERY
--------------------------------------------------

The sculpture wears classical draped fabric over the shoulders and upper torso.

Model the garment rather than leaving the bust completely bare.

Required:
- fabric draped over both shoulders
- deep sculpted folds
- flowing fabric valleys and ridges
- cloth gathered near the shoulders
- classical Greco-Roman sculpture appearance

Include the circular fastening ornament / brooch visible near the shoulder.

The drapery should have strong sculptural folds similar to marble carving.

Do NOT make the garment a flat smooth shirt.

--------------------------------------------------
7. BUST TERMINATION
--------------------------------------------------

Create a proper classical bust form.

Include:
- head
- neck
- shoulders
- upper chest
- partial upper torso
- clean sculptural termination at the bottom

Do not create a full human body.

--------------------------------------------------
8. SURFACE STYLE
--------------------------------------------------

The entire final sculpture should read as one carved stone / marble artwork.

Geometry should carry the main detail.

Do not rely on textures to fake:
- facial forms
- blindfold folds
- hair grooves
- clothing folds

Use real modeled/sculpted geometry.

Material:
single neutral white marble / plaster material for preview.

No skin shader.
No colored hair.
No metallic accessories.
No modern materials.

--------------------------------------------------
9. BLENDER MODEL STRUCTURE
--------------------------------------------------

Keep major parts editable.

Recommended objects:

Bust_Body
Head
Blindfold_Cloth
Hair_Front
Hair_Crown
Hair_Back
Hair_Long_Locks
Drapery
Shoulder_Brooch

Use clean subdivision-compatible geometry or clean sculpt/remesh geometry where appropriate.

Avoid:
- floating accidental geometry
- intersecting surfaces
- open holes
- broken normals
- unnecessary micro-detail

--------------------------------------------------
10. MOST IMPORTANT VISUAL FEATURES
--------------------------------------------------

The final silhouette must immediately communicate:

CLASSICAL FEMALE MARBLE BUST
+
HEAD TILTED UPWARD
+
FABRIC BLINDFOLD COVERING THE EYES
+
SCULPTED WAVY / BRAIDED HAIR
+
LONG ELEGANT NECK
+
CLASSICAL DRAPERY OVER THE SHOULDERS

The current model fails mainly because:
- the face is missing
- the blindfold looks like a helmet
- the hair looks like a smooth cap
- the head angle is incorrect
- classical drapery is missing
- the overall anatomy is too simplified

Correct all of these.

FINAL PRIORITY:
1. Match the reference silhouette
2. Correct upward head pose
3. Accurate classical female face
4. Cloth blindfold with visible folds
5. Sculpted hair masses
6. Neck / shoulder anatomy
7. Classical drapery
8. Fine details

Do not simplify these major features.

steps.prompt:
Create a clean 3D hard-surface sci-fi panel/module asset based on the provided reference image.

IMPORTANT:
- Model geometry only.
- Do NOT create or assign any materials.
- All materials should be NONE.
- The final model must be grouped according to visually separable material-like regions from the reference image, even though no actual materials are applied.

==================================================
1. OVERALL OBJECT
==================================================

The asset is a single futuristic mechanical panel / wall-mounted or ceiling-mounted module.

The overall silhouette is a thick wedge-like box form:
- a large main body
- a slanted front / underside panel area
- a relatively clean top surface
- a more detailed front-lower face

Do not redesign the object.
Preserve the overall proportion and silhouette from the reference image.

==================================================
2. PRIMARY FORM
==================================================

The object should be modeled as:
- one large main body mass
- a top panel section
- a slanted front-lower detailed panel section
- small mounting / bracket-like protrusions
- one top vent area
- one central horizontal bar-like detail
- secondary hard-surface framing details

The model should remain a single asset, not multiple unrelated objects.

==================================================
3. TOP AREA
==================================================

The top area is relatively simple.

Include:
- a flat top panel
- panel segmentation on the top
- a centered elongated vent/slit detail
- slightly beveled surrounding surfaces

Do not overcomplicate the top surface.

==================================================
4. FRONT / LOWER MAIN PANEL
==================================================

The front-lower face is the most detailed area.

It should include:
- angular panel segmentation
- polygonal hard-surface divisions
- beveled edges
- recessed line details
- framed surface sections
- a centered structural feel

This area should read as a futuristic hard-surface mechanical cover panel.

Keep the large shapes readable.
Do not fill the surface with excessive tiny noise.

==================================================
5. CENTRAL DETAIL
==================================================

Include a horizontal bar-like detail near the upper part of the front-lower face.

Also include:
- small support-like pieces around this bar
- a central lower small mechanical connector-like detail
- angled ribs or framed structures guiding toward the center

==================================================
6. SMALL PROTRUSIONS
==================================================

Include the small bracket / clip / mounting-like protrusions visible around the bottom edge and upper edge areas.

These should remain simple and readable.

Do not invent extra complex mechanical parts.

==================================================
7. DETAIL STYLE
==================================================

Use a clean sci-fi hard-surface modeling language.

Focus on:
- large and medium forms first
- crisp panel divisions
- bevels
- inset / recessed hard-surface details
- structural clarity

Avoid:
- excessive greeble detail
- unnecessary pipes
- exposed inner machinery
- cables
- random small bolts everywhere

==================================================
8. MATERIALS
==================================================

Do not assign materials.
Do not texture.
Do not create shader-based detail.

All material slots should remain empty / none.

==================================================
9. GROUPING
==================================================

Even though no materials are assigned, group the model according to visual material-style separation from the reference image.

Use separate groups/components for at least:

- Main_Body
- Top_Panel
- Top_Vent
- Front_Main_Panel
- Center_Bar_Detail
- Structural_Frame_or_Ribs
- Brackets_Clips
- Small_Secondary_Details

This grouping is important for later material assignment.

==================================================
10. MODEL QUALITY
==================================================

The model must be clean and editable.

Requirements:
- clean hard-surface geometry
- no unnecessary internal geometry
- no floating broken parts
- no open holes unless clearly intended
- good readable topology for modeling workflow
- suitable for later export to SketchUp / Blender / Unreal workflow

==================================================
11. FINAL INTENT
==================================================

The result should be a simple but well-defined sci-fi hard-surface module asset that closely matches the reference image.

Preserve the silhouette and major details.
Do not use materials.
Group the model by visually separable material-like parts for future workflow.

steps.title: 프롬프트
steps.prompt:
[ASTRA 6 MEDIUM — HIGH PRECISION REFERENCE-BASED 3D MODELING]

TASK:
Reconstruct ONE modular perforated ceiling panel from the attached multi-view reference sheet.

This is a geometry reconstruction task, NOT a creative redesign task.

The final model must follow the supplied reference as closely as possible in:

- overall dimensions
- proportions
- panel thickness
- frame width
- frame depth
- recessed layers
- perforation layout
- corner construction
- edge details
- backside construction
- side profile

Do NOT redesign, stylize, simplify, exaggerate, or add new details that are not supported by the reference.

============================================================
A. REFERENCE PRIORITY
============================================================

Use the reference views with the following priority:

1. DIMENSIONED ORTHOGRAPHIC VIEWS
2. FRONT / BACK / LEFT / RIGHT VIEWS
3. TOP / BOTTOM VIEWS
4. DETAIL CALLOUTS
5. PERSPECTIVE VIEW

The perspective image is only a visual aid.

When perspective appearance conflicts with the orthographic dimensions,
ALWAYS follow the orthographic views and written dimensions.

Do NOT model:

- text
- labels
- arrows
- dimension lines
- reference borders
- graphic layout
- shadows
- reflections
- lighting
- background

Only model the physical ceiling panel.

============================================================
B. REAL-WORLD DIMENSIONS
============================================================

Use exact real-world scale.

OVERALL PANEL SIZE:

X = 1200 mm
Y = 600 mm
Z = 40 mm

Do not change the aspect ratio.

The final bounding size must remain:

1200 × 600 × 40 mm

Tolerance target:
within approximately ±2 mm for the main outer dimensions.

============================================================
C. PRIMARY OBJECT DEFINITION
============================================================

The object is a thin rectangular modular ceiling panel.

It consists of four major physical systems:

01. OUTER PERIMETER FRAME
02. RECESSED PERFORATED PANEL
03. REAR / INTERNAL SOLID PANEL
04. SMALL EDGE / JOINT / FASTENER DETAILS

The center is NOT a thick solid slab.

The visible perforated surface must sit inside the surrounding frame.

The panel must have layered construction and visible depth.

============================================================
D. OUTER FRAME — STRICT GEOMETRY
============================================================

Create a continuous rectangular perimeter frame.

The outer frame must:

- follow the exact 1200 × 600 mm footprint
- have approximately 40 mm total panel thickness
- surround all four sides
- have real physical thickness
- contain a visible inner recess
- include a stepped edge profile
- include subtle mechanical corner transitions

Do NOT model the frame as a single flat rectangular extrusion.

The profile must contain multiple depth levels.

Required visual structure:

OUTER EDGE
→ SHALLOW RECESSED STEP
→ INNER FRAME/LIP
→ PERFORATED INSERT

Maintain consistent frame width around the perforated field unless the
reference clearly shows a local mechanical variation.

============================================================
E. CORNER CONSTRUCTION
============================================================

The four corners must not look like primitive box corners.

Use the corner detail reference.

Each corner should contain:

- clean 90-degree perimeter construction
- subtle stepped or layered metal profile
- localized seam / joint language
- slight hard-surface bevels
- precise panel-to-frame transition

Do NOT invent oversized sci-fi armor pieces.

The design language must remain:

minimal
industrial
modular
precise

Corner details must remain secondary to the main frame.

============================================================
F. PERFORATED PANEL — VERY IMPORTANT
============================================================

The perforated central area is a PRIMARY geometric feature.

Create the perforations as REAL 3D GEOMETRY.

DO NOT use:

- texture-only holes
- opacity map
- bump map
- normal map
- fake black squares
- surface decals

Each perforation must physically pass into / through the perforated panel.

Target specification from the reference:

HOLE SHAPE:
square

APPROXIMATE HOLE SIZE:
8 mm × 8 mm

APPROXIMATE PITCH:
12 mm center-to-center

APPROXIMATE GAP:
4 mm between adjacent openings

APPROXIMATE DEPTH:
12 mm

The hole grid must:

- remain perfectly aligned
- use constant spacing
- remain parallel to panel edges
- stop cleanly before the inner frame
- maintain uniform border clearance

Do not allow holes to intersect the frame.

Do not create partially cut holes at the outer boundary.

If the exact number of holes cannot perfectly match because of reference
ambiguity, prioritize:

1. correct panel size
2. correct 12 mm pitch
3. approximately 8 mm hole size
4. symmetrical and centered grid
5. clean border margin

============================================================
G. PERFORATION TOPOLOGY
============================================================

Keep the perforated panel efficient and clean.

Preferred method:

- create one clean panel surface
- generate an even square grid
- create repeated physical cutouts
- maintain consistent wall thickness
- avoid duplicate internal surfaces

All perforations must have:

- vertical interior walls
- clean top opening
- clean lower termination
- consistent depth

Do NOT create distorted or tapered holes unless clearly visible in reference.

Do NOT randomly vary hole size.

Do NOT add dents, noise, damage, or surface imperfections.

============================================================
H. PERFORATED PANEL RECESS
============================================================

The perforated panel must sit slightly recessed relative to the outer frame.

Do not place the perforated surface flush with the highest outer edge.

The relationship should read visually as:

outer perimeter frame
↓
inner recessed lip
↓
perforated mesh surface

This depth separation must be modeled physically.

Do NOT rely on material contrast to create this separation.

============================================================
I. REVERSE / INTERNAL SIDE
============================================================

Use the BOTTOM VIEW / INTERNAL SIDE reference.

The reverse side is primarily a solid rectangular panel.

Create:

- solid backside panel
- perimeter structural members
- shallow recessed construction
- visible support rails if shown
- small circular / mechanical fastener points

The backside must NOT reproduce the perforated grid.

The perforated surface belongs to the visible perforated face only.

Do not make both sides perforated.

============================================================
J. BACK PANEL
============================================================

Create the rear/internal panel as a separate physical object.

It must:

- fit inside the perimeter structure
- remain flat and clean
- follow the dimensions shown in the reference
- sit at the correct depth within the 40 mm total profile
- contain only the visible structural details shown in the sheet

Avoid unnecessary internal engineering parts that are not visible.

============================================================
K. FASTENERS
============================================================

The reference shows small fastener / screw-like points on the internal side.

Model these only where clearly visible.

They should be:

- small
- shallow
- precisely placed
- secondary details

Do not exaggerate them.

Do not create complex screw threads.

A shallow circular or mechanical recessed fastener representation is enough.

Each fastener may remain a separate object if appropriate.

============================================================
L. EDGE JOINT / LATCH DETAILS
============================================================

Use the FRAME DETAIL and side views.

Create the small modular notch / latch-like details visible along the outer frame.

Important:

These are subtle mechanical details.

Do NOT transform them into:

- handles
- large hinges
- large brackets
- protruding machinery

They should remain integrated into the shallow frame profile.

Keep them aligned with the edge.

============================================================
M. SIDE PROFILE
============================================================

Use FRONT, BACK, LEFT, and RIGHT views to reconstruct the 40 mm profile.

The profile must remain very thin compared to 1200 × 600 mm plan dimensions.

Do NOT make the panel bulky.

From the side, the model should show:

- upper frame layer
- recessed central layer
- lower/back structural layer
- subtle joint details

The final silhouette from the side should remain close to the reference.

============================================================
N. BEVEL RULES
============================================================

Use small realistic hard-surface bevels only where required.

Bevels should:

- catch edges
- clarify the layered frame
- maintain industrial fabrication logic

Do NOT use large soft bevels.

Do NOT make the object look rounded.

Do NOT bevel every internal perforation excessively.

Keep edges mostly crisp.

============================================================
O. SYMMETRY RULES
============================================================

The primary rectangular structure should remain symmetrical.

The following should be centered and aligned:

- overall panel
- perforation field
- major inner frame
- backside main panel

However:

Do not automatically mirror local latch / fastening features if the reference
shows different placement.

Reference accuracy has priority over procedural symmetry.

============================================================
P. NO MATERIALS
============================================================

IMPORTANT:

This task is GEOMETRY ONLY.

Do not assign any actual materials.

Do not create:

- metal material
- black material
- aluminum material
- steel material
- plastic material
- paint
- texture
- roughness
- normal map
- metallic value
- emissive
- transparency

ALL OBJECTS:

Material = NONE / Default / Unassigned

The model must be delivered completely material-free.

============================================================
Q. OBJECT SEPARATION
============================================================

Do NOT collapse everything into one object.

Physically separate major parts.

Recommended object structure:

OBJ_FRAME_TOP
OBJ_FRAME_BOTTOM
OBJ_FRAME_LEFT
OBJ_FRAME_RIGHT

OBJ_FRAME_CORNER_TL

OBJ_FRAME_CORNER_BL

OBJ_EDGE_DETAIL_03
OBJ_EDGE_DETAIL_04

OBJ_FASTENER_01
OBJ_FASTENER_02
OBJ_FASTENER_03
...

Do not separate every individual perforation into a separate selectable object.

The perforated field should remain one manageable perforated panel object.

============================================================
R. REQUIRED GROUPING HIERARCHY
============================================================

Grouping is mandatory.

The hierarchy must follow this exact logic:

INDIVIDUAL OBJECT
→ COMPONENT GROUP
→ MATERIAL GROUP
→ MASTER GROUP

Because there are no actual materials,
use MAT_NONE only as an organizational parent group.

Required hierarchy:

MASTER_CEILING_PANEL_TYPE_A
│
└── MAT_NONE
    │
    ├── GRP_OUTER_FRAME

============================================================
S. GROUPING LOGIC — STRICT
============================================================

The required logic is:

Geometry
→ Individual Object
→ Component Group
→ MAT_NONE
→ MASTER_CEILING_PANEL_TYPE_A

Do NOT use:

MASTER
→ FRONT
→ BACK
→ LEFT
→ RIGHT

T. TOPOLOGY QUALITY
============================================================

Required:

- no non-manifold geometry
- no loose edges
- no duplicate faces
- no coplanar overlapping surfaces
- no unnecessary internal faces
- no inverted normals
- no accidental open boundaries
- no zero-area faces
- no floating vertices
- no unnecessary triangulation on flat areas

Avoid excessive polygon count outside the perforation geometry.

U. MODELING EFFICIENCY
============================================================

Spend polygon density where it matters:

HIGH PRIORITY:
- perforated geometry

LOW PRIORITY:

- extremely small surface imperfections
- microscopic bevel segmentation

V. NORMALS / SURFACE QUALITY
============================================================

ONE accurately reconstructed modular ceiling panel.

steps.title: 프롬프트
steps.prompt:
[ASTRA 6 MEDIUM — HIGH PRECISION SPIRAL HANDRAIL MODELING]

TASK:
Create ONLY the handrail / guardrail system shown in the attached Rhino reference images.

The reference images show the same helical / spiral stair geometry from multiple viewpoints.

Use all provided views together to reconstruct the railing path accurately.

IMPORTANT:
The stair itself is reference geometry only.

DO NOT remodel the staircase.
DO NOT remodel the stair treads.
DO NOT remodel the central stair structure.

Create ONLY:

1. vertical railing posts / balusters
2. continuous upper handrail
3. necessary connection geometry between the posts and handrail

The final output must be suitable for SketchUp (.SKP).

============================================================
1. PRIMARY REFERENCE LOGIC
============================================================

The railing must follow the exact outer path of the spiral staircase visible in the Rhino reference images.

Do NOT replace the existing geometry with a generic circular spiral.

Do NOT create a mathematically perfect helix unless it matches the reference.

Use the reference geometry to determine:

- railing horizontal path
- spiral curvature
- vertical progression
- start point
- end point
- local changes in direction
- relationship between each stair tread and railing post
- continuous handrail trajectory

The reference stair geometry defines the railing path.

The railing should visually align with the outer perimeter of the stair.

============================================================
2. FIXED DIMENSIONS — DO NOT MODIFY
============================================================

The following dimensions are fixed and must be followed exactly.

RAILING HEIGHT:
15 mm

HANDRAIL THICKNESS:
1.5 mm

Do NOT scale these dimensions automatically.

Do NOT reinterpret them based on architectural standards.

Use the values exactly as specified.

============================================================
3. RAILING HEIGHT
============================================================

Every vertical railing post must rise:

15 mm

vertically from its corresponding mounting position.

Measure the height vertically in world Z direction.

Do NOT measure 15 mm along the slope of the staircase.

Correct:

base point
→ vertical Z direction
→ 15 mm

All primary railing posts should have consistent height unless the reference clearly requires a different termination condition.

============================================================
4. HANDRAIL
============================================================

Create a continuous upper handrail following the top points of the vertical railing posts.

HANDRAIL THICKNESS:
1.5 mm

Prefer a clean circular section unless the reference geometry clearly indicates another profile.

Recommended:

circular handrail
diameter = 1.5 mm

The handrail must:

- remain continuous
- follow the helical stair path
- maintain smooth curvature
- pass through or connect consistently to the top of the posts
- maintain the same section size throughout
- rise continuously with the staircase

Do NOT create the handrail as disconnected short segments.

The visual result must read as ONE continuous flowing rail.

============================================================
5. HANDRAIL PATH
============================================================

The handrail path is extremely important.

Follow the outer edge of the stair path shown in the reference.

The handrail must reproduce:

- circular / spiral progression in plan
- vertical progression in elevation
- multiple turns around the central axis
- transitions between each stair level
- top and bottom termination points

Do not flatten the handrail.

Do not make the rail horizontal.

Do not create separate circular rings for each level.

It must be one continuous three-dimensional spiral curve.

============================================================
6. VERTICAL POSTS / BALUSTERS
============================================================

Create vertical posts along the outer stair edge as shown in the reference.

Each post must:

- remain vertical in world Z
- begin at the outer stair / railing base position
- extend upward exactly 15 mm
- connect to the continuous upper handrail

Do NOT tilt the posts to follow the stair slope.

Posts remain vertical.

The stair and rail rise around them.

============================================================
7. POST POSITIONING
============================================================

Use the Rhino reference images to determine post positions.

Posts appear repeatedly along the outer edge of the stair.

Prioritize alignment with the stair modules / tread locations visible in the reference.

Do NOT distribute the posts randomly.

Do NOT create arbitrary equal spacing if it conflicts with the reference.

Where possible:

one repeated post position should correspond consistently to the stair module pattern.

Maintain the visual rhythm shown in the original Rhino model.

============================================================
8. POST PROFILE
============================================================

Keep the posts simple.

Do not create decorative railing posts.

Use a minimal straight structural profile.

Unless another profile is clearly visible in the reference, use a simple narrow circular or rectangular section.

The railing must remain visually lightweight.

Do NOT make the posts excessively thick.

Do NOT introduce ornamental details.

============================================================
9. PLAN VIEW ACCURACY
============================================================

The supplied top view is critical.

Use it to preserve the circular / helical plan geometry.

The railing path must maintain the correct relationship between:

- inner stair opening
- stair outer perimeter
- outer railing path

The railing must remain on the OUTER side of the spiral stair.

Do not move the railing toward the center opening.

Do not change the spiral radius arbitrarily.

============================================================
10. ELEVATION ACCURACY
============================================================

Use the side and perspective views to reconstruct the vertical progression.

The railing must rise continuously with the staircase.

Preserve the number of visible spiral rotations and the approximate pitch shown in the references.

Do NOT compress the vertical spacing.

Do NOT stretch the spiral vertically.

Do NOT change the number of turns.

Use the Rhino images as the primary geometric reference.

============================================================
11. START / END CONDITIONS
============================================================

Follow the visible start and end points from the reference.

At the lowest stair:

terminate the railing cleanly at the beginning of the stair flight.

At the highest stair:

terminate the handrail cleanly at the end of the visible stair flight.

Do not extend the rail beyond the reference.

Do not add decorative end caps unless necessary for closed geometry.

============================================================
12. GEOMETRY REQUIREMENTS
============================================================

All railing parts must be actual 3D geometry.

Do NOT use:

- lines only
- curves only
- construction guides
- 2D profiles without thickness

The final SKP model must contain physical solid geometry.

Handrail:
closed tubular or solid profile

Posts:
closed solid geometry

No open faces.

No broken surfaces.

============================================================
13. CURVE QUALITY
============================================================

The continuous upper handrail must appear smooth.

Use enough segments to preserve the spiral curve when imported into SketchUp.

However:

Do NOT create excessive segmentation.

Avoid unnecessarily dense geometry.

Use an efficient curve resolution that maintains a visually smooth handrail.

Avoid faceted or visibly polygonal curvature.

============================================================
14. OBJECT SEPARATION
============================================================

Do NOT merge the entire railing into one raw mesh.

Each primary physical component must remain independently editable.

Recommended individual objects:

OBJ_HANDRAIL_MAIN

OBJ_POST_001
OBJ_POST_002
OBJ_POST_003
OBJ_POST_004
OBJ_POST_005
...

If multiple disconnected handrail sections are truly necessary:

OBJ_HANDRAIL_SECTION_01
OBJ_HANDRAIL_SECTION_02

However, prefer one continuous handrail whenever possible.

============================================================
15. REQUIRED GROUP HIERARCHY
============================================================

Use a clean SketchUp-compatible hierarchy.

Required logic:

INDIVIDUAL GEOMETRY
→ INDIVIDUAL OBJECT / GROUP
→ COMPONENT GROUP
→ MAT_NONE
→ MASTER GROUP

Required hierarchy:

MASTER_SPIRAL_HANDRAIL
│
└── MAT_NONE
    │
    ├── GRP_HANDRAIL
    │   └── OBJ_HANDRAIL_MAIN
    │
    └── GRP_VERTICAL_POSTS
        ├── OBJ_POST_001
        ├── OBJ_POST_002
        ├── OBJ_POST_003
        ├── OBJ_POST_004
        ├── OBJ_POST_005
        └── ...

Every vertical post must remain individually selectable.

Do not explode all posts into raw geometry.

============================================================
16. MATERIAL RULES
============================================================

NO MATERIALS.

This task is geometry only.

Do not assign:

- metal
- steel
- black material
- white material
- glass
- paint
- texture
- color
- roughness
- metallic shader
- emissive material

All geometry must use:

Material = NONE / Default / Unassigned

MAT_NONE is only a hierarchy / organizational group.

MAT_NONE is NOT an actual material.

============================================================
17. SKETCHUP REQUIREMENTS
============================================================

The final model will be used directly in SketchUp.

Therefore:

- keep every post as a separate group/component
- keep the main handrail as a separate group
- prevent raw geometry from sticking to adjacent geometry
- avoid unnecessary nested groups
- use clear object names
- maintain editable geometry
- preserve real-world dimensions
- keep axes consistent
- ensure correct face orientation

All front faces should point outward.

No reversed faces should remain visible.

============================================================
18. MODEL CLEANUP
============================================================

Before export, verify:

- no duplicate posts
- no overlapping handrail geometry
- no disconnected handrail segments
- no floating vertices
- no loose edges
- no duplicate faces
- no internal accidental faces
- no non-manifold geometry
- no broken circular profiles
- no unnecessary triangulation
- no accidental merged stair geometry

============================================================
19. DO NOT MODEL THE STAIRS
============================================================

This is extremely important.

The stair visible in the reference images is ONLY used to determine the railing path.

DO NOT include:

- stair treads
- risers
- staircase frame
- central column
- floor slabs
- staircase support structure

Final output:

HANDRAIL / GUARDRAIL ONLY.

============================================================
20. DO NOT ADD NEW DESIGN ELEMENTS
============================================================

Do not add:

- horizontal middle rails
- glass panels
- wire cables
- mesh panels
- decorative rail elements
- brackets not shown
- extra balusters
- ornamental elements

Reproduce only the railing system visible in the Rhino reference.

============================================================
21. PRIORITY ORDER
============================================================

If any reference information is ambiguous, use this priority:

1. fixed dimensions supplied in the prompt
2. top-view railing trajectory
3. vertical progression visible in side views
4. post positions visible in multiple views
5. perspective appearance

Never override:

15 mm railing height
1.5 mm handrail thickness

============================================================
22. FINAL ACCEPTANCE CHECK
============================================================

Before finalizing, verify:

[ ] Only railing geometry was modeled

[ ] Stair geometry was NOT included

[ ] Railing follows the outer perimeter of the reference staircase

[ ] Spiral trajectory matches the supplied Rhino views

[ ] Number of spiral turns matches the reference

[ ] Vertical progression matches the reference

[ ] All posts are vertical

[ ] Every post height = exactly 15 mm

[ ] Handrail thickness = exactly 1.5 mm

[ ] Upper handrail is continuous

[ ] Handrail follows the top of the vertical posts

[ ] No random post placement

[ ] Individual posts are separately selectable

[ ] Handrail is separately selectable

[ ] Geometry is grouped correctly

[ ] All objects are inside component groups

[ ] All component groups are inside MAT_NONE

[ ] MAT_NONE is inside MASTER_SPIRAL_HANDRAIL

[ ] No material is assigned

[ ] No texture is assigned

[ ] No extra design elements are added

[ ] Geometry is clean and SketchUp-ready

FINAL OUTPUT:

ONE clean spiral handrail / guardrail assembly based on the supplied Rhino reference.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
SKP

MODEL:
HANDRAIL ONLY

FIXED DIMENSIONS:
RAILING HEIGHT = 15 mm
HANDRAIL THICKNESS = 1.5 mm

MATERIAL:
NONE

GEOMETRY:
CLEAN, EDITABLE, GROUPED

NO CREATIVE REDESIGN.
DO NOT MODIFY THE REFERENCE SPIRAL TRAJECTORY.

TASK

Using the six supplied reference images, reconstruct this sci-fi hard-surface
column as a clean, editable SketchUp model.

The objective is NOT to create a visually similar interpretation.

The objective is to reconstruct the visible geometry, proportions,
panel divisions and mechanical structure of the supplied references
as faithfully and consistently as possible.

The final model will later be manually textured/materialized by me
and may subsequently be exported to Unreal Engine.


==================================================
REFERENCE IMAGE ROLES
==================================================

Use the images according to the following roles:

01_END_A.png
- Primary reference for the geometry of one end of the object
- Use for footprint, corner positions, major frame geometry,
  central circular assembly and X-shaped structural layout

02_PERSPECTIVE_A.png
- Secondary depth reference
- Use to understand protrusions, recesses, connections
  and relationships between the side panels and end structure

03_PERSPECTIVE_B.png
- Secondary depth reference
- Use together with Perspective A to understand depth,
  overlapping parts and mechanical connections

04_SIDE_A.png
- Primary reference for vertical proportions
- Use for total height-to-width ratio
- Use for vertical panel divisions
- Use for top and bottom transition geometry
- Use for locations of rails, bolts and major side components

05_SIDE_B.png
- Primary reference for the adjacent side
- Use to verify symmetry and vertical alignment
- Use to identify differences between adjacent faces

06_END_B.png
- Primary reference for the opposite end
- Use for opposite-end geometry, frame layout,
  recessed areas and central mechanical assembly


==================================================
REFERENCE PRIORITY
==================================================

When different images appear to conflict, NEVER randomly average them.

Use the following priority rules:

1. END images control end footprint and plan geometry.
2. SIDE images control vertical proportions and elevations.
3. PERSPECTIVE images control depth, recesses and connections only.
4. Small decorative discrepancies have lower priority than the
   main silhouette and structural geometry.

Do not use perspective distortion to determine absolute width or height.


==================================================
IMPORTANT LIMITATION
==================================================

No absolute real-world dimension has been provided.

Therefore:

- preserve the proportions shown in the references
- do not invent real-world dimensions
- work in millimeters
- keep the entire model uniformly scalable
- do not claim absolute dimensional accuracy

If an overall dimension is later provided, the entire model must be
capable of being uniformly rescaled without reconstruction.


==================================================
MODELING METHOD
==================================================

This is a hard-surface mechanical model.

Build the model using clean SketchUp-native geometry.

Do NOT create a chaotic triangulated mesh.

Use:

- planar faces
- clean extrusions
- controlled bevels
- simple mechanical solids
- repeated components where appropriate

Prefer simple geometry that accurately reproduces the visible shape.


==================================================
SYMMETRY
==================================================

The object appears to contain substantial four-way rotational symmetry.

Where the reference images confirm identical geometry:

1. Model one repeated module accurately.
2. Make it a SketchUp Component.
3. Rotate-copy it in 90-degree increments around the vertical center axis.

Do NOT separately remodel identical repeated components.

This is required to reduce geometric inconsistency.

However:

Do NOT force symmetry onto an area if the reference images clearly show
that the geometry is different.


==================================================
PRIMARY FORM FIRST
==================================================

Model in this order:

STEP 1
Overall bounding volume and proportions

STEP 2
Main vertical body

STEP 3
Top/end assembly

STEP 4
Bottom/opposite-end assembly

STEP 5
Large dark structural frames

STEP 6
Vertical mechanical rails and recessed areas

STEP 7
Major panel divisions

STEP 8
Central circular mechanical components

STEP 9
Large bolts and connectors

STEP 10
Secondary details and bevels

Do not begin with screws or decorative details.


==================================================
SILHOUETTE ACCURACY
==================================================

The external silhouette has the highest priority.

Accurately reproduce:

- overall column proportions
- widened upper transition
- widened lower transition
- chamfered corner geometry
- end-frame geometry
- central vertical recesses
- major frame thicknesses
- major panel boundaries

Do not redesign the silhouette.


==================================================
PANEL GEOMETRY
==================================================

The large light-colored panels shown in the references must be modeled
as actual separate panel geometry or clearly separated face regions.

Preserve:

- panel boundaries
- recessed black center channels
- major panel joints
- top and bottom transition plates
- visible panel gaps

Do not merge the entire side into one undifferentiated surface.


==================================================
RECESSES AND OPENINGS
==================================================

Pay particular attention to all black recessed mechanical areas.

A dark area in the reference does NOT automatically mean an open hole.

If a recess is visible but there is no evidence that it passes completely
through the object:

create a shallow or appropriate-depth recess with a rear surface.

Do NOT create infinite open cavities.

All intentional recesses must contain:

front opening
→ side walls
→ rear/back surface

unless the reference clearly shows a true through-hole.


==================================================
CLOSED GEOMETRY
==================================================

No accidental holes are allowed.

Any cavity exposing an undefined empty interior must be closed with
simple internal/back geometry.

All major exterior parts should be watertight / solid groups whenever practical.

Do not leave open rear faces simply because they are not visible
from one reference image.


==================================================
DO NOT INVENT HIDDEN DETAIL
==================================================

Do not invent complex internal machinery that is not visible.

For ambiguous hidden areas:

use the simplest reasonable geometry that connects the visible surfaces
and preserves the exterior appearance.

Do NOT add random:

- pipes
- vents
- cables
- sci-fi decorations
- extra armor
- unnecessary holes
- mechanical mechanisms

unless they are supported by the supplied references.


==================================================
DEPTH ESTIMATION
==================================================

Use both perspective images to estimate:

- panel thickness
- rail protrusion
- frame depth
- recessed channel depth
- end-cap thickness
- mechanical overlap

Depth must remain visually consistent on all four sides.

Avoid exaggerated depth that exists only because of perspective distortion.


==================================================
BEVEL / CHAMFER
==================================================

The model must not consist entirely of perfectly sharp 90-degree edges.

Apply small controlled bevels/chamfers to major visible hard-surface edges.

Use bevels particularly on:

- outer corner frames
- upper and lower structural frames
- panel borders
- central mechanical assemblies
- large rails
- large mechanical blocks

Do not create excessive bevel segments.

Use low-to-moderate segmentation appropriate for SketchUp.


==================================================
FASTENERS
==================================================

Visible bolts and circular fasteners are secondary geometry.

Create a small number of reusable bolt Components.

Reuse Components instead of rebuilding every fastener.

Keep them reasonably low-poly.

Do NOT model microscopic screw threads.

Do not allow bolts to penetrate randomly through unrelated geometry.


==================================================
MATERIALS
==================================================

I will apply all final materials myself.

DO NOT create final materials or textures.

DO NOT create:

- PBR materials
- normal maps
- roughness maps
- metallic maps
- emissive materials
- texture maps

Keep the geometry in SketchUp Default Material.

Do not paint individual faces with arbitrary colors.


==================================================
GEOMETRY SEPARATION
==================================================

Although no final materials are required,
geometry that is likely to receive different materials later
must remain independently selectable.

Use approximately this hierarchy:

SCI_FI_COLUMN_MASTER

01_MAIN_BODY
    Main_Panels

02_DARK_STRUCTURAL_FRAME
    Upper_Frame
    Lower_Frame
    Corner_Frames

03_VERTICAL_MECHANICAL
    Vertical_Rails
    Recessed_Center_Parts

04_END_A_ASSEMBLY
    EndA_Frame
    EndA_Center
    EndA_Mechanical

05_END_B_ASSEMBLY
    EndB_Frame
    EndB_Center
    EndB_Mechanical

06_HARDWARE
    Bolts
    Circular_Fasteners
    Connectors

07_BACK_PLATES
    Recess_Back_Plates

Each category must remain independently selectable.

Do not merge everything into one raw mesh.


==================================================
SKETCHUP GROUPING RULES
==================================================

Every significant geometry set must belong to a Group or Component.

No loose geometry should remain at the top model level.

Use Components for repeated parts such as:

- repeated corner structures
- repeated rails
- repeated fasteners
- rotationally repeated details

Do not create hundreds of unnecessary one-face Groups.

Grouping should follow meaningful construction or future material zones.


==================================================
FACE ORIENTATION
==================================================

All exterior faces must point outward.

Inspect and correct reversed faces.

No visible exterior surface may use a reversed back face.

This is important for later Unreal Engine export.


==================================================
COPLANAR / DUPLICATE GEOMETRY
==================================================

There must be no duplicate or perfectly overlapping coplanar faces.

Avoid Z-fighting.

Remove:

- duplicated surfaces
- duplicated edges
- overlapping panels
- accidental internal copies
- floating edges
- isolated vertices
- unnecessary hidden geometry


==================================================
INTERSECTIONS
==================================================

Components may physically connect,
but unrelated solids must not randomly pass through each other.

Check all intersections around:

- top frame
- bottom frame
- corner panels
- vertical black rails
- circular center mechanisms
- fasteners

Correct unintended penetration.


==================================================
MICRO DETAIL
==================================================

Do not model tiny surface details that do not meaningfully affect silhouette.

Do NOT model:

- surface grain
- scratches
- printed warning symbols
- tiny labels
- tiny engraving
- microscopic panel gaps
- microscopic bolt detail

These will be handled later with materials/textures.

Model only geometric detail that produces a visible shape or shadow.


==================================================
AXIS / ORIGIN
==================================================

Use Z as the vertical axis.

Center the main object on the SketchUp world origin.

Place the lowest physical point of the object on Z = 0.

Keep the center axis aligned with the SketchUp vertical axis.

Do not model the white background or floor.


==================================================
QUALITY CONTROL
==================================================

Before finalizing the model, perform a complete inspection from:

- End A
- End B
- Side A
- Side B
- Perspective A
- Perspective B

Compare the SketchUp model against all six references.

First check silhouette.

Then check:

1. overall proportions
2. end footprint
3. panel positions
4. widened top transition
5. widened bottom transition
6. central recess locations
7. rail alignment
8. frame thickness
9. rotational symmetry
10. circular connector positions
11. bolt positions
12. recess depth
13. bevel consistency


==================================================
GEOMETRY VALIDATION
==================================================

Before saving, verify:

1. No unintended open holes
2. No missing rear/back surfaces
3. No reversed exterior faces
4. No loose raw geometry
5. No duplicate faces
6. No coplanar overlapping faces
7. No random intersections
8. No unnecessary internal geometry
9. Repeated geometry uses Components
10. Similar elements have consistent dimensions
11. All four sides align correctly
12. The model is centered
13. The bottom is at Z = 0
14. The model remains easy to edit
15. Geometry can be assigned materials later without remodeling


==================================================
FINAL RULE
==================================================

Accuracy is more important than decorative detail.

Do not reinterpret the design.

Do not make the model "more sci-fi."

Do not add creative details.

When a reference is ambiguous, use the simplest geometry consistent with
the other five images.

Preserve:

SILHOUETTE
→ PROPORTION
→ STRUCTURAL LAYOUT
→ PANEL LAYOUT
→ DEPTH
→ MAJOR DETAIL

in that exact priority order.
한 가지는 내가 추가로 강하게 권장함

Astra에게 처음부터 끝까지 한 번에 만들라고 하지 않는 것이 좋음.

위 프롬프트 마지막에 이것도 붙이는 걸 추천함.

일반 텍스트
WORKFLOW REQUIREMENT

Do not attempt to finish the entire detailed model immediately.

First create only:

1. overall massing
2. bounding proportions
3. major top/end geometry
4. major bottom/end geometry

Then compare the blockout against all six reference images.
