steps.title: 03-B · 작성된 프롬프트와 안내 원문 (답변)
steps.prompt:
ChatGPT 답변:

좋습니다. 아래는 크레딧 제출용으로 바로 붙여넣을 수 있는 영어 프롬프트입니다.

일반 텍스트
[REFERENCE-BASED 3D MODELING TASK]

Create a 3D model of the futuristic sci-fi installation structure based on the attached reference image.

Important:
The goal is not simply to recreate the render visually, but to build a clean hard-surface 3D model that can be edited later in SketchUp and Unreal Engine.

Preserve the overall silhouette, proportions, and structural relationships of the reference image as closely as possible.

==================================================
1. Overall Structure
==================================================

The structure is a futuristic vertical installation organized around a central axis.

From bottom to top, the structure consists of:

1) base platform frame  
2) central vertical core  
3) cable and support system around the core  
4) small central cube  
5) large upper cube  
6) extended vertical luminous core above

Everything must be aligned along a single central vertical axis.

As in the reference image, the large cube should appear suspended above the ground.

A smaller cube is positioned directly below the large cube.

Both cubes must share the same center axis.

==================================================
2. Large Upper Cube
==================================================

The upper mass is a near-cubic form.

Add a thin black metal frame around the outer edges.

Some faces should be transparent glass, while some inner faces should be black or dark semi-transparent panel surfaces.

Important:
Do not combine the glass and black panel parts into a single object.

Each surface must be created as a separate object.

Examples:

TOP_GLASS_FRONT  
TOP_GLASS_LEFT  
TOP_GLASS_RIGHT  
TOP_GLASS_BOTTOM  

TOP_BLACK_PANEL_FRONT  
TOP_BLACK_PANEL_LEFT  
TOP_BLACK_PANEL_RIGHT  

TOP_FRAME_VERTICAL_01  
TOP_FRAME_VERTICAL_02  
TOP_FRAME_HORIZONTAL_01  
...

The frame should be modeled as a realistic thin square-profile metal structure.

Inside the cube, add a limited number of thin linear light panels and small digital panel-like elements similar to the reference.

Do not over-model extremely tiny decorative details.

==================================================
3. Small Central Cube
==================================================

Create a smaller dark cube centered directly below the large upper cube.

Its visual size should be approximately 1/3 to 1/4 of the upper cube.

The smaller cube must also be separated into:

- black panel elements  
- transparent glass elements  
- thin metal frame elements

Do not model any text or logos.

Remove the words such as "DON'T WORRY" and "EVERYTHING IS OK" from the structure.

==================================================
4. Central Vertical Core
==================================================

Create a vertical rectangular or square core passing through the center of the structure.

The core should connect continuously from the base upward through:

BASE  
→ SMALL CUBE  
→ LARGE CUBE  
→ ABOVE LARGE CUBE

Also create a separate emissive mesh for the glowing cyan / ice-blue light effect.

Important:

Separate the structural core and the emissive core.

Examples:

CORE_STRUCTURE  
CORE_EMISSIVE_FRONT  
CORE_EMISSIVE_LEFT  
CORE_EMISSIVE_RIGHT  

==================================================
5. Lower Cable System
==================================================

From the underside of the small central cube, create multiple cables descending outward toward the base platform.

The cables should have a smooth natural curved shape.

Do not merge all cables into one mesh.

Examples:

CABLE_01  
CABLE_02  
CABLE_03  
CABLE_04  
...

If necessary, add small connector brackets or anchor parts at the cable ends.

The cables must have a visible 3D thickness and should not be modeled as ultra-thin lines.

==================================================
6. Base Platform
==================================================

Remove all grass, vegetation, soil, landscaping, and rail-like surrounding elements from the reference.

ONLY THE STRUCTURE.

The final result must show only the installation itself.

Create a simple square or rectangular platform at the bottom.

Add a thin black metal frame around the perimeter.

Around the central core, include only minimal structural supports and brackets as needed.

The base should be divided as follows:

BASE_FLOOR  
BASE_FRAME_FRONT  
BASE_FRAME_BACK  
BASE_FRAME_LEFT  
BASE_FRAME_RIGHT  

BASE_SUPPORT_01  
BASE_SUPPORT_02  
...

Do not add any landscaping or decorative environment.

==================================================
7. Modeling Rules
==================================================

All geometry must be created as closed 3D solid / manifold mesh geometry.

Do not create:

- open surfaces  
- non-manifold geometry  
- overlapping duplicate faces  
- unnecessary internal faces  
- loose geometry  
- accidentally merged objects  
- automatic single-mesh combination  
- vegetation  
- grass  
- background elements  
- people  
- furniture  
- surrounding architecture

Glass must not be a simple plane without thickness.
It must be modeled as a thin solid object.

Metal frame parts must also have real physical thickness.

==================================================
8. Required Group Hierarchy
==================================================

This is the most important requirement.

The hierarchy must be organized in the following order:

[Individual Object]
→ [Material Group]
→ [Master Group]

Geometry must not be placed directly inside a material group.

Every piece of geometry must first be made into its own individual object group.

Example hierarchy:

MASTER_STRUCTURE
│
├── MAT_CLEAR_GLASS
│   │
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_GLASS_FRONT
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_GLASS_LEFT
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_GLASS_RIGHT
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_GLASS_BOTTOM
│   │
│   ├── OBJ_SMALL_GLASS_FRONT
│   ├── OBJ_SMALL_GLASS_LEFT
│   └── OBJ_SMALL_GLASS_RIGHT
│
├── MAT_BLACK_GLASS
│   │
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_BLACK_PANEL_FRONT
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_BLACK_PANEL_LEFT
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_BLACK_PANEL_RIGHT
│   ├── OBJ_SMALL_BLACK_PANEL_FRONT
│   ├── OBJ_SMALL_BLACK_PANEL_LEFT
│   └── OBJ_SMALL_BLACK_PANEL_RIGHT
│
├── MAT_BLACK_METAL
│   │
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_FRAME_01
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_FRAME_02
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_FRAME_03
│   ├── OBJ_SMALL_FRAME_01
│   ├── OBJ_SMALL_FRAME_02
│   ├── OBJ_BASE_FRAME_FRONT
│   ├── OBJ_BASE_FRAME_BACK
│   ├── OBJ_BASE_FRAME_LEFT
│   ├── OBJ_BASE_FRAME_RIGHT
│   ├── OBJ_SUPPORT_01
│   └── OBJ_SUPPORT_02
│
├── MAT_EMISSIVE_CYAN
│   │
│   ├── OBJ_CORE_LIGHT_FRONT
│   ├── OBJ_CORE_LIGHT_LEFT
│   ├── OBJ_CORE_LIGHT_RIGHT
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_LIGHT_01
│   ├── OBJ_TOP_LIGHT_02
│   └── OBJ_BASE_LIGHT
│
├── MAT_CORE_STRUCTURE
│   │
│   └── OBJ_VERTICAL_CORE
│
├── MAT_CABLE_BLACK
│   │
│   ├── OBJ_CABLE_01
│   ├── OBJ_CABLE_02
│   ├── OBJ_CABLE_03
│   ├── OBJ_CABLE_04
│   ├── OBJ_CABLE_05
│   └── OBJ_CABLE_06
│
└── MAT_BASE_FLOOR
    │
    └── OBJ_BASE_PLATFORM

Do NOT organize the model like this:

MASTER
→ TOP CUBE
→ geometry

or:

MASTER
→ all glass geometry

These structures are not allowed.

The required structure must always be:

Geometry
→ Individual Object Group
→ Material Group
→ MASTER_STRUCTURE

==================================================
9. Material Classification
==================================================

At minimum, create the following 7 material categories:

01_CLEAR_GLASS  
02_BLACK_GLASS  
03_BLACK_METAL  
04_CORE_STRUCTURE  
05_EMISSIVE_CYAN  
06_BLACK_CABLE  
07_BASE_FLOOR  

Each individual object should generally contain only one material.

If one object needs more than one material, split it into separate objects.

Incorrect:
FRAME_AND_GLASS_01

Correct:
FRAME_01  
GLASS_01  

==================================================
10. Pipeline Considerations
==================================================

This model will be used later in SketchUp and Unreal Engine.

Therefore:

- every object must be named  
- all material groups must be separated  
- each object must be individually selectable  
- minimize unnecessary triangulation  
- keep surfaces as clean as possible  
- avoid unnecessary vertices on flat surfaces  
- use only the necessary number of segments for curved cables  
- avoid excessive subdivision  
- place the model center at world origin  
- use the bottom center of the structure as 0,0,0  
- use Z-up orientation

==================================================
11. Final Visual Identity
==================================================

The final result should clearly read as:

"a large suspended glass cube
+ a smaller central dark cube
+ a vertical luminous core
+ exposed cables
+ a minimal structural platform"

The overall feeling should be:

minimal / futuristic / sci-fi / technological installation

However, do not redesign it too freely.

Prioritize the silhouette and structural proportions of the attached reference image.

NO GRASS  
NO VEGETATION  
NO LANDSCAPE  
NO TEXT  
NO HUMAN  
NO BACKGROUND OBJECTS  

ONLY THE ARCHITECTURAL / MECHANICAL STRUCTURE.

원하면 내가 이어서 바로
1) 더 짧은 버전
또는
2) Astra 6에 넣기 좋은 최적화 버전
으로 다시 정리해드릴게요.

steps.prompt:
PROJECT TYPE
Architectural environment detailing in Blender for final use in Unreal Engine 5.

PRIMARY GOAL
Use the provided existing 3D site model as the fixed spatial base and develop it into a highly detailed architectural environment using the provided reference image as the MODELING DETAIL reference.

The reference image is NOT only a mood, lighting, color, or material reference.
Its architectural geometry, modular detailing, terrain treatment, floor articulation, ceiling articulation, cubic elements, recesses, openings, rock formations, and spatial density must be translated into the existing site.

The final result must remain fully editable in Blender and must be organized for clean Unreal Engine 5 export.

==================================================
1. PROVIDED INPUTS
==================================================

Use all provided files/images together:

1. Existing 3D base model
   - Use this as the absolute spatial and dimensional reference.
   - Preserve the original real-world scale.
   - Preserve the existing site boundary.
   - Preserve existing major building positions.
   - Preserve major circulation paths.
   - Preserve major terrain positions.
   - Preserve the overall composition and footprint.

2. Existing model Top View image
   - Use this to verify site organization, circulation, boundaries, building locations, and terrain placement.

3. Existing model Perspective View image
   - Use this to verify existing massing, relative height, terrain relationships, and overall spatial composition.

4. Target Reference Image
   - Use this specifically as the MODELING DETAIL REFERENCE.
   - Extract its architectural detailing language and apply it to the provided site.
   - Do NOT simply copy the reference image as a completely new environment.
   - Adapt its detailing system to the geometry of the existing project.

==================================================
2. ABSOLUTE PRESERVATION RULES
==================================================

DO NOT:

- redesign the entire site
- change the site boundary
- rescale the entire project
- move the major buildings
- arbitrarily rotate the project
- significantly modify the main circulation structure
- replace the existing project with a new reference-inspired site
- change the main architectural massing unless required for secondary detailing
- destroy recognizable existing terrain composition
- flatten the existing site
- convert everything into one merged mesh
- generate one giant monolithic object
- create decorative geometry unrelated to the reference
- model reflections
- model fake shadows
- model fake light rays
- model reflected geometry visible in glass
- bake visual reflections into geometry
- model the contents of reflections
- create unnecessary hidden geometry

The existing project must remain recognizable.

REFERENCE MODEL = FIXED BASE
TARGET REFERENCE = DETAILING LANGUAGE

==================================================
3. DESIGN LANGUAGE TO EXTRACT FROM REFERENCE
==================================================

Translate the following characteristics into the existing model:

- dense modular architectural landscape
- dark monolithic architectural masses
- highly articulated floor surface
- stepped terrain integrated into architecture
- cubic modular interventions
- square voids and recessed floor openings
- embedded cubic elements
- projecting cubic elements
- recessed facade cubes
- solid cubes
- translucent-style cube geometry
- perforated cubes
- ribbed cubes
- metallic cube modules
- illuminated cube placeholders
- irregular natural rock formations
- controlled contrast between natural rock and strict cubic geometry
- modular wall openings
- recessed facade pockets
- ceiling panels
- ceiling service-like modules
- linear ceiling recesses
- long narrow ceiling slots
- lighting channels integrated into architectural geometry
- subtle bevels on hard-surface edges
- dense but organized spatial detail
- repeating components with controlled variation

The environment must feel intentionally designed, not randomly scattered.

==================================================
4. FLOOR SYSTEM
==================================================

Develop the floor as a major architectural element.

Create:

A. Main floor surfaces
B. Secondary raised floor zones
C. Lower recessed zones
D. Stepped circulation zones
E. Modular floor panel divisions
F. Square floor openings
G. Recessed square pockets
H. Linear lighting recess geometry
I. Step-edge lighting recess geometry
J. Selective floor grilles / perforated panels where appropriate

The floor must NOT remain as one flat continuous surface.

Use the reference image to create a controlled rhythm of:

flat floor
→ slight level change
→ step
→ recessed square
→ solid floor
→ modular opening
→ terrain transition

Maintain clear walkable circulation.

Do not cover major circulation routes with excessive obstacles.

Avoid random holes.

Floor openings must follow the architectural grid and overall spatial logic.

==================================================
5. FLOOR OPENINGS
==================================================

Create selected square and rectangular openings similar to the reference.

Requirements:

- clean Boolean geometry
- proper depth
- actual physical openings or recesses
- no coplanar overlapping faces
- no zero-thickness surfaces
- no fake black planes pretending to be holes
- edge thickness must be visible
- internal side walls must exist
- bottom geometry must exist when the opening is a recess rather than a complete void

Vary opening sizes in a controlled modular system.

Do not make every opening identical.

==================================================
6. STEP AND TERRACE SYSTEM
==================================================

Use architectural steps and terraces to increase spatial depth.

Steps should:

- follow the existing terrain and circulation
- integrate with the current model
- remain realistically walkable where intended
- contain clean risers and treads
- include optional linear lighting recesses at selected edges
- avoid excessive repetition
- maintain clear human-scale circulation

Do not transform the whole site into stairs.

Use steps only where they reinforce terrain transitions and spatial hierarchy.

==================================================
7. TERRAIN REFINEMENT
==================================================

Retain the existing terrain positions and overall terrain composition.

Refine the existing terrain in Blender.

Convert overly smooth or generic terrain into more believable sculpted landforms.

Create a mixture of:

- soft terrain slopes
- exposed rock
- sharper rock cuts
- eroded edges
- layered rock transitions
- smaller secondary stone formations
- architectural floor penetrating into terrain
- terrain penetrating slightly into architectural zones

Avoid:

- perfect blobs
- overly inflated forms
- melted-looking terrain
- cartoon rock
- uniform noise
- random displacement everywhere

Terrain must have controlled directional structure.

==================================================
8. ROCK FORMATIONS
==================================================

The reference contains natural rock formations integrated with architectural elements.

Create multiple rock assets rather than one repeated rock.

Minimum recommended rock variation:

Rock_A_Large
Rock_B_Large
Rock_C_Medium
Rock_D_Medium
Rock_E_Small

Rock requirements:

- asymmetric silhouette
- believable geological mass
- irregular but controlled surface
- broad planar breaks
- medium-scale fracture
- restrained micro-detail
- no excessive procedural noise
- no identical repeated rocks

Rock geometry may use relatively high polygon density because the final target is Unreal Engine 5 and Nanite compatibility is expected.

However, geometry must remain structurally clean.

==================================================
9. CUBIC MODULAR SYSTEM
==================================================

Create a reusable modular cube asset system inspired by the reference.

Create separate master modules:

Cube_Solid
Cube_Glass
Cube_Perforated
Cube_Ribbed
Cube_Metal
Cube_Stone
Cube_Light
Cube_Recessed
Cube_Protruding

Do NOT model every cube from scratch.

Use master objects and linked duplicates / instances wherever possible.

Create controlled dimensional variations.

Suggested logic:

small
medium
large

Do not make all cubes the exact same size.

Do not scatter cubes randomly.

Use cubes to:

- mark circulation
- create spatial rhythm
- integrate into buildings
- emerge from floor zones
- integrate with terrain
- create focal points
- form facade modules

==================================================
10. PERFORATED CUBE
==================================================

Perforated cubes must contain actual architectural detail.

Requirements:

- clean outer cube form
- repeated perforation system
- consistent perforation spacing
- believable structural edge thickness
- perforations aligned to the cube faces
- avoid millions of unnecessary holes

If actual geometry becomes excessively dense, use an optimized modular perforated face system.

Do not use a simple flat image as the only representation if the perforations affect silhouette or close-range viewing.

==================================================
11. RIBBED CUBE
==================================================

Create ribbed cubic modules inspired by the reference.

Requirements:

- clean repeated vertical or horizontal fins
- consistent spacing
- clearly visible depth
- proper corner termination
- no intersecting ribs
- no floating pieces
- no accidental gaps

Use instance-based repetition where possible.

==================================================
12. TRANSLUCENT / GLASS CUBE GEOMETRY
==================================================

Create only the physical geometry required for glass/translucent cube objects.

DO NOT:

- model reflections
- model interior reflected objects
- duplicate the environment inside the cube
- create fake mirrored geometry
- create reflection geometry

The final Unreal material will handle transparency and reflections.

Blender only needs:

- clean closed geometry
- correct normals
- appropriate wall thickness where required
- separate glass material slot

==================================================
13. BUILDING DETAILING
==================================================

Retain the main building masses.

Add secondary architectural detailing inspired by the reference.

Possible additions:

- square recesses
- deep window-like cavities
- cube insertions
- projecting boxes
- recessed boxes
- modular facade panels
- perforated inserts
- ribbed inserts
- small architectural pockets
- selected vertical slots
- selected lighting recesses

Do NOT completely rebuild or reshape the major buildings.

Use the existing buildings as hosts for the new modular detailing system.

Facade details must maintain structural visual logic.

Avoid random checkerboard decoration.

==================================================
14. CEILING SYSTEM
==================================================

The ceiling is an important part of the reference.

Create a modular ceiling system.

Include:

- large ceiling panel fields
- secondary rectangular panels
- recessed panels
- narrow linear slots
- long service-like grilles
- ventilation-style panels
- lighting recess channels
- selected dropped modules
- controlled panel variation

Do not make the ceiling perfectly flat and empty.

Do not create excessive visual noise.

Maintain a clear hierarchy:

Main Ceiling
→ Large Panels
→ Secondary Panels
→ Service Grilles
→ Lighting Recesses

==================================================
15. LIGHTING GEOMETRY
==================================================

Only model the PHYSICAL GEOMETRY for lighting integration.

Create:

Floor_Light_Recess
Step_Light_Recess
Wall_Light_Recess
Ceiling_Light_Recess

These should be actual channels / slots / recesses.

Do NOT attempt to create the final Unreal lighting.

Do NOT bake final emission.

Do NOT create volumetric light geometry.

Do NOT create fake glowing meshes beyond simple placeholder geometry.

Actual lighting, emissive materials, Lumen, fog, and reflections will be created in Unreal Engine 5.

==================================================
16. VEGETATION
==================================================

Vegetation is NOT a primary Blender modeling requirement.

Do not spend significant time modeling final vegetation.

If vegetation is needed for spatial indication:

- use simple placeholders only
- keep them in a separate collection
- do not merge them with terrain
- ensure they can be deleted easily before Unreal export

Final vegetation will primarily be handled in Unreal Engine.

==================================================
17. MATERIAL RULES
==================================================

DO NOT create final materials or final textures.

DO NOT spend time creating final PBR shading.

Use neutral placeholder materials only.

Material separation is required.

Create material slots such as:

MAT_STONE
MAT_DARK_STONE
MAT_METAL
MAT_BLACK_METAL
MAT_GLASS
MAT_PERFORATED_METAL
MAT_RIBBED_METAL
MAT_EMISSIVE
MAT_CONCRETE
MAT_TERRAIN
MAT_VEGETATION

All placeholder materials may remain simple neutral colors.

The purpose of materials in Blender is ONLY:

- face/material classification
- Unreal material assignment
- object organization

No final look development is required.

==================================================
18. COLLECTION STRUCTURE
==================================================

Organize the Blender scene EXACTLY or very closely according to the following hierarchy:

00_REFERENCE_EXISTING
    Existing_Site
    Existing_Buildings
    Existing_Terrain
    Existing_Path

01_FLOOR
    Floor_Main
    Floor_Raised
    Floor_Recessed
    Floor_Steps
    Floor_Panels
    Floor_Openings

==================================================
19. OBJECT SEPARATION
==================================================

DO NOT join the entire environment into one mesh.

Keep logically different systems separate.

At minimum, keep the following independently editable:

- buildings
- floor
- steps
- terrain
- large rocks
- modular floor panels
- floor openings
- cube master assets
- cube instances
- facade detail
- ceiling
- ceiling panels
- lighting recess geometry

Objects using completely different material types should generally remain separate when practical.

==================================================
20. HARD-SURFACE MODELING QUALITY
==================================================

All architectural hard-surface geometry must have:

- clean topology
- correct face orientation
- correct normals
- no duplicated faces
- no internal accidental faces
- no non-manifold geometry unless intentionally open
- no accidental floating edges
- no zero-area faces
- no extremely thin accidental triangles
- no visible Boolean artifacts
- no overlapping coplanar surfaces

Use subtle bevels on exposed architectural edges where appropriate.

Do not leave infinitely sharp CG edges on major close-range objects.

Bevel size must remain proportional to object scale.

==================================================
21. TERRAIN TOPOLOGY
==================================================

Terrain and rock meshes may use denser geometry than architectural meshes.

However:

- avoid unnecessary ultra-dense geometry
- remove hidden duplicate surfaces
- preserve major silhouette quality
- keep terrain editable
- apply sculpt/remesh workflow carefully
- preserve transitions with architectural surfaces

Do not decimate so aggressively that the terrain becomes visibly faceted.

==================================================
22. UV REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Provide usable UVs for major final assets.

UV priority:

HIGH:
- buildings
- floor
- steps
- modular cubes
- facade panels
- ceiling panels

MEDIUM:
- rocks
- terrain

Do not create extremely distorted UVs.

For large architectural surfaces, use sensible texel distribution.

Final textures will be created or assigned later in Unreal Engine.

==================================================
23. MODIFIER RULES
==================================================

During modeling, non-destructive modifiers may be used.

Recommended:

- Mirror
- Array
- Bevel
- Boolean
- Solidify
- Subdivision where required
- Geometry Nodes where repetition is beneficial

Before final Unreal export:

- verify all modifiers
- apply modifiers only when required for stable FBX export
- preserve a Blender master version with editable modifiers where possible

==================================================
24. INSTANCE / REPETITION OPTIMIZATION
==================================================

Repeated assets must reuse master geometry whenever practical.

Especially:

- cubes
- floor panels
- ceiling panels
- grilles
- perforated modules
- ribbed modules
- repeated facade modules

Avoid creating hundreds of unique meshes containing identical geometry.

==================================================
25. HUMAN SCALE
==================================================

Maintain believable architectural scale.

Do not allow reference-inspired details to become oversized.

Check:

- step dimensions
- circulation width
- cube size
- facade opening size
- ceiling panel scale
- rock scale
- lighting recess width
- floor panel dimensions

The environment must remain usable and believable at human scale.

==================================================
26. CIRCULATION
==================================================

Maintain continuous primary circulation.

Do not place:

- cubes
- rocks
- openings
- terrain protrusions

in locations that completely block the intended circulation path.

Use detailed elements to frame circulation rather than destroy it.

Provide enough clear floor surface for a person to walk naturally through the environment.

==================================================
27. DETAIL DENSITY
==================================================

The reference has high visual density, but the result must remain controlled.

Use three levels of detailing:

PRIMARY
- major architecture
- terrain
- large rock formations
- major steps

SECONDARY
- floor modules
- facade recesses
- large cube installations
- ceiling modules

TERTIARY
- perforations
- ribs
- small cube variations
- small lighting recesses
- small floor details

Do not apply tertiary detail uniformly everywhere.

Create focal areas and quieter areas.

==================================================
28. REFERENCE INTERPRETATION RULE
==================================================

Do not recreate the reference image literally.

Instead extract its architectural system:

MODULAR GRID
+
CUBIC OBJECTS
+
ROCK / TERRAIN
+
RECESSES
+
STEPPED FLOOR
+
DARK MONOLITHIC MASSES
+
CEILING PANEL SYSTEM
+
INTEGRATED LIGHTING CHANNELS

and adapt this system to the existing project.

The final model must still match the spatial identity of the supplied base model.

==================================================
29. BLENDER SCENE CLEANUP
==================================================

Before completion:

- delete unused geometry
- delete hidden accidental duplicates
- remove orphan meshes where appropriate
- remove unused material slots
- rename all important objects
- organize all collections
- ensure visible objects are in correct collections
- check face normals
- check object scale
- check origins
- check transforms
- check mesh intersections
- check Boolean results
- check UVs
- check material assignment
- check Unreal export readiness

==================================================
30. TRANSFORM REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Maintain the existing global project coordinates unless export compatibility requires otherwise.

Do not arbitrarily center each building independently.

Preserve the complete site relationship.

For modular reusable assets:

- set logical origins
- preferably center or bottom-center depending on placement logic

For major site geometry:

- preserve world-space relationship

Verify:

Rotation
Scale
Location

before export.

==================================================
31. UNREAL ENGINE 5 READINESS
==================================================

The final Blender scene must be prepared specifically for Unreal Engine 5.

Optimize for:

- Static Mesh import
- Nanite-compatible high-detail meshes
- clean material-slot assignment
- clean object naming
- independent asset control
- correct normals
- usable UVs
- modular reuse
- predictable pivot placement
- collision generation later in Unreal

Do NOT unnecessarily reduce important rock or architectural silhouette detail only to achieve traditional low-poly optimization.

Nanite will be used where appropriate.

==================================================
32. COLLISION
==================================================

Do not create highly complex custom collision for every detailed object unless necessary.

Collision priority:

- main walkable floor
- steps
- buildings
- major rocks adjacent to circulation
- major architectural obstacles

Small visual details do not require complex Blender collision meshes unless specifically needed.

Keep collision geometry simple.

==================================================
33. EXPORT
==================================================

Maintain a master .blend file.

Final required deliverables:

1. Fully editable Blender master file
2. Unreal-ready FBX export

Recommended final file names:

PROJECT_MASTER.blend
PROJECT_UE5.fbx

FBX export must preserve:

- object separation
- object names
- transforms
- material slots
- hierarchy where possible
- correct normals
- full site spatial relationship

Do not collapse everything into one object.

==================================================
34. FINAL VISUAL TARGET
==================================================

The final Blender viewport should clearly show the MODELING complexity of the target reference even WITHOUT final textures or final lighting.

The quality must come from geometry:

- articulated terrain
- detailed floor
- rock formations
- steps
- recesses
- cubic architecture
- modular cube system
- facade articulation
- ceiling articulation
- embedded lighting channels

It must NOT rely on:

- final material quality
- fake reflections
- dramatic rendering
- heavy post-processing
- volumetric effects

The geometry itself must be strong enough to read clearly in a neutral clay viewport.

==================================================
35. FINAL QUALITY CONTROL
==================================================

Before finishing, perform a final inspection from:

TOP VIEW
FRONT-LEFT PERSPECTIVE
FRONT-RIGHT PERSPECTIVE
LOW HUMAN-EYE VIEW
OVERALL AERIAL VIEW

Confirm all of the following:

[ ] Existing site composition preserved
[ ] Major building positions preserved
[ ] Existing terrain logic preserved
[ ] Circulation remains usable
[ ] Reference modeling language clearly visible
[ ] Floor no longer appears generic or flat
[ ] Terrain has believable detail
[ ] Rock formations are varied
[ ] Cubic system has multiple module types
[ ] Cubes are not randomly scattered
[ ] Facades have controlled recess/projection detail
[ ] Ceiling has architectural articulation
[ ] Lighting recess geometry exists
[ ] No reflection geometry exists
[ ] No final materials are required
[ ] Material slots are correctly separated
[ ] Objects are organized into collections
[ ] Repeated assets reuse master geometry
[ ] Normals are correct
[ ] Topology is clean
[ ] UVs are usable
[ ] No accidental duplicated geometry
[ ] No major mesh intersections
[ ] Unreal export structure is clean
[ ] Full project remains at correct real-world scale

FINAL PRIORITY ORDER:

1. PRESERVE ORIGINAL SITE / SCALE
2. PRESERVE MAJOR ARCHITECTURAL COMPOSITION
3. ADD REFERENCE-LEVEL MODELING DETAIL
4. CREATE STRONG TERRAIN + ROCK INTEGRATION
5. CREATE MODULAR CUBE SYSTEM
6. CREATE ARTICULATED FLOOR SYSTEM
7. CREATE FACADE AND CEILING DETAIL
8. ORGANIZE EVERYTHING FOR UNREAL ENGINE 5
9. KEEP MATERIALS AS PLACEHOLDERS ONLY
10. DELIVER CLEAN EDITABLE BLENDER + FBX

steps.title: 02-B · 작성된 프롬프트와 안내 원문 (답변)
steps.prompt:
ChatGPT 답변:

이 장면을 뜯어보면 필요한 에셋은 대략 5종류야. 완성형 하나를 찾기보다는, 아래 구성요소를 따로 가져와 조합하는 게 훨씬 현실적이야.

등고선형 계단/벤치 에셋
장면 오른쪽의 핵심 요소야. 가장 가까운 건 parametric bench / topographic seating / contour bench 계열. Sketchfab의 Parametric Seating 2는 무료 다운로드 가능하고, 미래적 곡면 좌석을 베이스로 수정하기 좋아. 
스케치팝

Parametric Seating 2 보기

또 다른 무료 후보는 PARAMETRIC BENCH인데, Blender modifier 기반이라 형태 수정성이 좋아. 
스케치팝

PARAMETRIC BENCH 보기

다만 네 이미지처럼 계단식 등고선이 바닥과 일체화된 형태는 완전히 동일한 판매 에셋보다, 이런 벤치를 베이스로 Blender에서 확장하는 게 더 맞아.

중앙의 유기적인 둔덕/언덕 매스
검색 결과 중 Earth Mound 같은 지형형 3D 모델은 있지만, 네 장면은 자연 흙더미보다 매끈한 건축적 조형물에 가까워. 
CGTrader

그래서 이 부분은 외부 에셋보다 Blender Sculpt / Subdivision / Metaball 또는 Rhino-Grasshopper로 만드는 편을 추천해.

참고용 검색어는:
organic architectural mound 3d model
futuristic sculptural mound
topographic interior landscape
smooth concrete landscape 3d

검은 대리석 큐브
이건 바로 가져다 쓸 후보가 있어. Marble Stand가 블랙 마블 큐브/스탠드 계열이고 FBX, OBJ도 제공돼. 
CGTrader

Marble Stand 보기

사실 형상 자체는 단순 큐브라서 네 작업에서는 직접 큐브 생성 + Black Marble PBR 적용이 더 빠를 수도 있어.

반투명 발광 큐브
장면에 있는 하얗게 빛나는 투명 큐브와 가장 가까운 무료 후보로 GLOWING CUBE가 있어. 기본적인 발광 큐브 에셋이고 무료로 제공돼. 
CGTrader

Glowing Cube 보기

Sketchfab의 Sci-Fi Energy Cube도 저폴리 발광 큐브라 언리얼 Lumen 테스트용으로 만들어진 모델이야. 
스케치팝

Sci-Fi Energy Cube 보기

바닥 사각 매입조명
장면 바닥에 뚫린 사각형에서 빛이 올라오는 부분. CGTrader의 Recessed Light – Game Ready가 가장 바로 쓰기 편해 보여. FBX/OBJ/GLTF/UAsset까지 있고 PBR 텍스처와 Emissive도 포함돼. 
CGTrader

Recessed Light 보기

Sketchfab에서도 무료 Recessed Light 모델이 있어. 
스케치팝

무료 Recessed Light 보기

네 장면 기준 조합 추천

나는 이렇게 구성하는 게 제일 효율적이라고 봐.

등고선 계단 → Parametric Seating 베이스를 변형
큰 둔덕 → 직접 모델링
검은 큐브 → 기본 Cube + Black Marble
투명 큐브 → Glowing Cube 계열
바닥 사각 발광부 → Recessed Light 에셋
벽/바닥 라인 조명 → 메시를 찾기보다 Unreal에서 Emissive Strip으로 직접 제작

특히 오른쪽 등고선 구조가 이 공간의 캐릭터를 거의 결정하니까, 여기는 에셋을 그대로 쓰기보다는 Parametric Seating을 가져와서 네 평면에 맞게 길이와 굴곡을 수정하는 게 좋아.

Pinterest에서 찾을 때는 아래 키워드가 잘 맞을 거야:

futuristic contour seating / topographic seating interior / parametric landscape bench / LED contour steps / futuristic terrain interior / organic concrete landscape interior

원하면 다음엔 내가 이 장면 기준으로 “무료 에셋만” 추려서 Sketchfab·CGTrader 위주로 10개 정도 직접 링크까지 골라줄 수 있어.

steps.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: presentation-ready architectural circulation and visual-field analysis diagram for a design panel/report
Primary request: Redesign the circulation overlay on the supplied floor plan. Preserve the floor plan and program locations, remove the crude thick black route, and replace it with an elegant analytical circulation diagram matching the visual language of the second reference.
Input images:
- Image 1 is the geometry authority and edit target. Preserve its exact top-down plan proportions, walls, angled perimeter, entrance at the lower-right, three lower hologram installations, the long central SF panel zone, the upper row of 3D-printer workstations and diagonal structural elements.
- Image 2 is style reference only. Borrow its thin brick-red route with many small directional chevrons, rust-red circular event nodes, translucent violet viewing cones, fine violet triangulated sight-line meshes, faint gray construction lines, and warm off-white architectural-paper atmosphere. Do not copy its building geometry.
Circulation sequence and exact route logic:
1. Begin at the lower-right entrance. The red path enters upward, bends left, and travels through the lower exhibition zone, weaving smoothly past the three pyramid hologram installations. This phase represents auditory data becoming visual through the holograms.
2. At the left side, curve upward into the central corridor. Continue from left to right along the full length of the long central SF empty-panel zone. Use a steady sequence of small red arrowheads to show forward movement and several pause nodes where the ceiling-panel audio is activated only while standing in position.
3. At the far right, make a broad U-turn upward, then travel from right to left through the upper 3D-printer experience zone, ending at the upper-left side. This phase connects the visitor's auditory data to visible 3D-printed output.
Visual-field logic:
- Add translucent purple viewing cones and triangulated meshes from selected red visitor nodes toward the relevant installations.
- In phase 1, aim the purple cones toward the pyramid holograms.
- In phase 2, use narrower elongated purple fields aligned with the central SF panels, showing focused attention and stationary listening points.
- In phase 3, fan purple fields from the upper route toward the individual 3D-printer stations.
- Sight fields may overlap softly but must remain secondary to the red route.
Style/medium: refined hand-drawn architectural analysis, precise fine-line diagram, research-atelier aesthetic, layered but legible.
Composition/framing: wide landscape top-down plan, centered with generous margins. One unified diagram, not multiple panels.
Color palette: black and soft gray plan linework; muted brick-red and rust-orange circulation; translucent lavender, violet, and blue-purple sight fields; warm ivory background.
Text: no labels, no words, no pseudo-text. Use only geometric nodes, route arrows, meshes, and linework.
Constraints: preserve the recognizable plan from Image 1; route must remain in walkable areas, never cross walls or solid furniture; clearly show one continuous direction from lower-right entrance to lower holograms to central SF panels to upper 3D-printer zone and upper-left finish; make red and purple graphics crisp enough for a report panel.
Avoid: thick black arrows, cartoon style, photorealism, 3D perspective, filled opaque color blocks, random decorative lines, illegible text, logos, watermark.

steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: A polished photorealistic material art-direction board for a proposed Unreal Engine 5.7.4 indoor planting material set. This is a visual concept, not an engine render and not a set of ready-to-import textures.
Primary request: Using the provided architectural scene as the main visual reference, design six plant-related material concepts compatible with the existing dark architectural material library. Plant geometry is being made separately; focus on material appearance, surface detail, color, and light response.
Input images: Image 1 is ONLY a reference for the planting palette and architectural mood, not an edit target. Image 2 is ONLY a reference for the existing ZIP library's cool grey concrete surface family and restrained material presentation, not an edit target.
Composition: Landscape presentation board, approximately 3:2 aspect ratio, clean restrained professional layout with six equally sized specimen panels in a 3-column by 2-row grid. Each panel has a large, extremely clear macro specimen and a small natural flat color patch at its lower corner. A narrow header and footer; ample margins; all six samples fully inside frame. Use physical specimen shapes appropriate to each material rather than identical material spheres. Neutral charcoal/slate presentation background. Large readable understated off-white typography.
Exact text: Header "PLANT MATERIAL STUDY"; subtitle "14–19 / INDOOR PLANTING"; panel captions exactly "14  BROADLEAF", "15  FERN", "16  MOSS", "17  BARK", "18  DAMP SOIL", "19  WEATHERED ROCK"; footer "VISUAL CONCEPT — NOT AN ENGINE RENDER". No other text or metrics.
Panel 14: Small cluster of plausible oval shrub leaves, muted deep forest green, thin natural veins, subtle waxy satin highlights, mature leaves with small controlled color variation. One gently curled leaf reveals a paler underside. Broadleaf surface must look alive but not glossy plastic.
Panel 15: Finely divided fern frond segment, slightly lighter desaturated olive green, slender separate leaflets, softer matte surface than broadleaf, convincing fine veins. Keep the fern visually distinct from the shrub.
Panel 16: A low dense patch of fine velvety moss on a compact sample of earth, restrained dark olive color, tiny varied filaments, irregular tuft edges, matte, no giant grass blades, no green glowing material.
Panel 17: A short slender grey-brown woody twig with fine longitudinal fibers and understated rough bark, proportions appropriate to a low shrub rather than a large tree trunk.
Panel 18: Exposed dark umber damp soil with fine grains, small irregular aggregates, only a few tiny organic fragments; moist but no standing water and no muddy mirror reflections. Rich readable microdetail.
Panel 19: A small naturally fractured grey mineral rock specimen, cool grey grain and fine pores, irregular weathering, subtly darkened damp crevices, one small sparse moss patch on an edge. Mineral stone, not metallic, no marble veins, no concrete casting marks.
Lighting: All six specimens under consistent broad diffuse neutral daylight, well exposed to evaluate actual greens and browns. Soft contact shadows and subtle grazing highlights. Do NOT bake the warm golden scene light into the specimen colors. The reference's warm ambience belongs in a separate scene study.
Palette: restrained forest green, olive green, grey brown bark, dark umber earth, cool grey rock, compatible with dark grey architecture. Natural, sophisticated, not oversaturated.
Quality and constraints: Photorealistic material research photography, exceptionally readable surface microstructure; no people, no flowers, no potted plants, no futuristic holographic blue effects, no neon, no decorative props. Do not invent PBR map diagrams or claim these samples are measured scans. Produce the concept board itself.

steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Photorealistic lighting-context concept board for six proposed indoor planting materials.
Primary request: Show how the proposed plant materials fit the user's architectural reference. Create a clear comparison of a compact planting pocket under neutral evaluation lighting and warm recessed architectural lighting. This is AI visual art direction, not an Unreal render or a controlled photometric test.
Input images: Image 1 is the architectural reference for setting, placement scale, and warm lighting mood. Image 2 is the approved material appearance reference for six materials: dark satin broadleaf, softer olive fern, matte moss, grey-brown slender twig bark, dark damp soil, naturally weathered grey stone. Neither input is an edit target; create a new comparison board.
Composition: Wide landscape, approximately 3:2 aspect ratio. Two equally sized side-by-side panels with a narrow margin, same approximately eye-level close three-quarter camera and matching arrangement of the small planting pocket in both panels. Planting occupies about 75 percent of each panel with very readable foliage; show the architectural border only as restrained context. No distant full-room view. Both panels should show the same materials, approximate plant poses and planting density so changes of lighting are easy to judge.
Scene: A low recessed planting bed at the base of a cool grey concrete wall alongside a dark grey stone curved stair edge and reflective charcoal floor. Low shrubs with small natural oval leaves on visible grey-brown twigs, a few distinct fine fern fronds in front, modest irregular moss patches around two small weathered grey stones, visibly dark granular moist earth between the plants. Respect the reference's low, sparse localized planting; no oversized tropical leaves, no overgrown jungle. No planters or pots. The rock should look mineral and irregular, not concrete. Stone and concrete are a quiet context, not the main subject.
Left panel: Broad diffuse neutral light lets the deep green leaf surfaces, olive fern details, matte moss, bark and soil read clearly. Leaf veins and stone pores visible; natural satin on broadleaf and lower sheen on fern. No bright white plastic reflection, no artificial leaf glow.
Right panel: The same planting arrangement lit from below and the side by a partly hidden warm white architectural strip with soft amber highlights, plus restrained cool ambient fill. Match the reference's welcoming warm/cool contrast. Warm light grazes a few leaf undersides and rock edges, with subtle leaf translucency, but foliage stays recognizably green in shadow and does not turn wholly brown or yellow. Deep shadows retain detail. Soil should remain matte damp, not lacquered. Golden glow is illumination only; the plants do not emit light.
Typography: Professional architectural art-direction layout, charcoal background, off-white restrained sans serif. Exact header "PLANTING / LIGHT RESPONSE". Left panel caption "NEUTRAL LIGHT". Right panel caption "WARM ARCHITECTURAL LIGHT". Exact footer "VISUAL CONCEPT — NOT AN ENGINE RENDER". No other text.
Constraints: Rich photorealistic texture, realistic microvariation, natural plausible leaves and ferns, no people, no flowers, no blue holograms, no extra decorative objects, no exaggerated bloom, no neon foliage, no water droplets, no claim of measured physical accuracy. Keep both compositions closely comparable.

steps.title: 01 · ROLE
steps.prompt:
ROLE
You are producing tileable PBR source textures for a photorealistic architectural
interior rendered in Unreal Engine 5.8 (Lumen, physically based lighting).
The images will be measured numerically and rejected if they fail the rules below.
Realism matters more than style: this must look like real, photographed/scanned
surfaces, NOT like a game or sci-fi concept art.

DELIVERABLES PER MATERIAL (3 files each)
  1. T_<Name>_BC.png  BaseColor / albedo
  2. T_<Name>_H.png   Height map
  3. T_<Name>_RV.png  Roughness-variation mask
  Do NOT produce normal, AO, roughness, metallic or ORM maps. They are derived later
  from the Height and RV maps so that all maps stay physically consistent.

GLOBAL RULES (apply to every file)
  - Perfectly SEAMLESS tiling on both axes. Left edge must continue into right edge,
    top edge into bottom edge, with no visible seam, no mirrored halves.
  - Square, power-of-two resolution exactly as specified (2048x2048 or 4096x4096).
  - Orthographic, straight top-down view of a FLAT surface. No perspective, no camera
    tilt, no vignetting, no lens effects, no depth of field.
  - The image covers exactly the stated PHYSICAL SIZE. Keep feature scale consistent
    with that size (e.g. 5 mm pores must be ~5 mm at that scale).
  - No text, logos, labels, watermarks, borders, UI, rulers or color charts.
  - No single large unique feature (one big stain, one big crack) that would make
    repetition obvious. Spread detail evenly; vary it at several scales
    (large soft variation, medium patches, fine grain).

BASECOLOR (_BC) RULES
  - Pure albedo, "delit": NO lighting, NO shadows, NO shading, NO ambient occlusion,
    NO specular highlights, NO reflections, NO sheen. Uniform flat illumination.
  - Brightness must be even across the whole image: the average of each quarter of
    the image must match the global average within +/-6 %. No gradients.
  - Neutral white balance unless the material description says otherwise.
  - 8-bit sRGB PNG, RGB (no alpha).
  - The MEAN sRGB value of the image must fall inside the stated range.

HEIGHT (_H) RULES
  - 16-bit grayscale PNG (8-bit accepted only if 16-bit is impossible).
  - Mid-gray (50 %) = the nominal flat surface. White = raised, black = recessed.
  - Only micro and meso surface relief (pores, orange-peel, brushing, grain, fine
    scratches). NO large bumps, NO panel seams, NO bevels, NO lighting baked in.
  - Use at least ~60 % of the tonal range so the relief is well quantized.
  - Must correspond to the same surface as the BaseColor (same pores / scratches in
    the same places).

ROUGHNESS-VARIATION (_RV) RULES
  - 8-bit or 16-bit grayscale PNG.
  - Black (0) = the cleanest / glossiest state of this material.
    White (255) = the most worn / dusty / matte state.
  - Content = how real use changes GLOSS, not color: foot-traffic wear paths,
    fingerprints and hand smears, dust accumulation, polishing swirls, water marks,
    fine scratches. Irregular, directional where appropriate, never a uniform
    cloud/Perlin noise.
  - Average around 25-40 % gray; most of the surface stays fairly clean, variation is
    concentrated in patches and streaks.
  - Must be seamless and aligned with the BaseColor/Height (same scratches).

FILE NAMES — use exactly these <Name> values:
  01 BlackEpoxy, 02 DarkConcrete, 03 WhitePaintedMetal, 04 DarkMetalPanel,
  05 BrushedAluminum, 06 BlackRubber, 07 PerforatedMetal, 08 CeilingMattePaint

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
MATERIAL 01 — BlackEpoxy  (polished black epoxy resin floor, commercial interior)
  Resolution: 4096 x 4096        Physical size: 200 cm x 200 cm
  BC: near-black neutral, MEAN sRGB 40-60 (target 50). Very subtle mottling of the
      resin, tiny embedded dust specks, faint lighter micro-scratches. No color tint.
  H : very fine orange-peel of a self-leveling coating (feature size 1-4 mm),
      scattered hairline scratches (0.1-0.5 mm wide, 2-20 cm long, random directions).
  RV: foot-traffic wear lanes (soft, elongated, mostly along one axis), scuff marks
      from shoes and trolleys, dust near random areas, light mop/polish swirl marks.

MATERIAL 02 — DarkConcrete  (smooth exposed cast-in-place concrete, dark gray)
  Resolution: 4096 x 4096        Physical size: 250 cm x 250 cm
  BC: dark-to-mid gray, MEAN sRGB 90-120 (target 104), slight cool-neutral.
      Cement tone variation in soft cloudy patches, small air-void pores (1-6 mm),
      faint darker water stains. No formwork tie holes, no panel joints.
  H : pores and bug-holes as small recesses, fine sandy grain, very soft waviness.
  RV: slightly glossier smoothed patches (trowel/formwork contact), matte dusty areas.

MATERIAL 03 — WhitePaintedMetal  (white powder-coated steel column cladding)
  Resolution: 2048 x 2048        Physical size: 100 cm x 100 cm
  BC: clean white, neutral, MEAN sRGB 200-230 (target 218). Extremely subtle
      tone variation only; no dirt streaks, no rust.
  H : powder-coat orange-peel texture (feature size 1-3 mm), very low amplitude.
  RV: fingerprints and hand smears at random spots, light dust, faint polishing marks.

MATERIAL 04 — DarkMetalPanel  (dark anthracite painted metal wall panel)
  Resolution: 4096 x 4096        Physical size: 150 cm x 150 cm
  BC: dark neutral gray, MEAN sRGB 55-75 (target 63). Very subtle paint tone
      variation, a few tiny lighter chips (< 2 mm). NO blue tint.
  H : fine satin paint texture, faint roller/spray pattern, tiny chips as recesses.
  RV: hand smears, light scuffs, dust on some areas.

MATERIAL 05 — BrushedAluminum  (satin brushed aluminium frame/trim)
  Resolution: 2048 x 2048        Physical size: 60 cm x 60 cm
  BC: bright neutral metal color, MEAN sRGB 225-250 (target 240). Nearly uniform;
      only extremely faint streaks aligned with the brushing. No reflections of
      anything, no dark/light banding from lighting.
  H : hairline brushing strictly along the HORIZONTAL (left-right) axis of the image.
      Long continuous fine lines, varied depth. No vertical or circular marks.
  RV: brushing-aligned streaks of slightly different gloss, a few fingerprints,
      light handling marks.

MATERIAL 06 — BlackRubber  (black synthetic rubber insert/strip)
  Resolution: 2048 x 2048        Physical size: 50 cm x 50 cm
  BC: black-charcoal neutral, MEAN sRGB 35-50 (target 44). Faint grayish dust bloom
      in places.
  H : fine matte grain/stipple (0.2-1 mm), soft micro-dents.
  RV: dust and wear patches that are slightly more matte, smoother rubbed spots.

MATERIAL 07 — PerforatedMetal  (black powder-coated steel sheet — SHEET ONLY)
  Resolution: 2048 x 2048        Physical size: 30 cm x 30 cm
  IMPORTANT: DO NOT DRAW ANY HOLES. Holes are generated separately and precisely.
             Produce only the continuous sheet surface.
  BC: black powder coat, MEAN sRGB 45-65 (target 56), neutral, very subtle variation.
  H : powder-coat orange-peel, faint rolling marks.
  RV: dust and light scuffs, slightly glossier rubbed spots.

MATERIAL 08 — CeilingMattePaint  (OPTIONAL — matte painted ceiling, dark gray)
  Resolution: 2048 x 2048        Physical size: 200 cm x 200 cm
  BC: dark neutral gray, MEAN sRGB 85-95 (target 90), almost uniform.
  H : very fine roller-paint stipple.
  RV: very subtle; mostly uniform with faint roller marks.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELF-CHECK BEFORE DELIVERY (please verify and report for each file)
  [ ] exact resolution and square
  [ ] seamless on both axes (check by offsetting the image by 50 % in X and Y)
  [ ] BC mean sRGB inside the range; quarter averages within +/-6 % of the mean
  [ ] BC has no lighting, shadows, highlights or reflections
  [ ] H is 16-bit grayscale, mid-gray = flat, uses >= 60 % of the range
  [ ] RV average 25-40 % gray, patchy/streaky (not uniform noise)
  [ ] BC, H and RV of the same material are spatially aligned
  [ ] PerforatedMetal contains NO holes; BrushedAluminum brushing is horizontal
==========================================================================
…

steps.title: 02-G1 · 이미지 생성 도구 호출 프롬프트 원문
steps.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Create one highly detailed photographic concept image of the PHYSICAL MINIATURE ARCHITECTURAL MODEL in input image 1, developed with the additional interior model-making details below. This is a tabletop student architecture exhibition maquette, not a full-size building, not a futuristic interior render.

Input roles:
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and the authoritative reference for the exact overall stepped acrylic-frame composition, silhouette, bay positions, suspended levels, large existing insert shapes, grey presentation plinth, frontal slightly elevated camera and miniature scale.
Image 2 is a supporting reference for the white room insert's panel divisions, layered door frames, perimeter benches, steps and thresholds.
Image 3 is a supporting reference ONLY for the idea of a touch-responsive floor/wall/ceiling. Translate it into simple static, physically fabricated miniature relief parts.
Image 4 is a supporting reference ONLY for the contour terrain and tactile cubes. Translate its geometry into WHITE LAYERED MODEL BOARD, not photoreal stone, vegetation or a full-size landscape.
Do not reproduce PDF page layouts, headings, text or collage panels.

Keep the original clear acrylic framework and original stepped arrangement from image 1, including the low single bay at far left, taller stack left of center, central deck stack, and raised two-bay platform on the right. Keep the existing principal white room, pyramid, diagonal structure and stair positions. Clear interior module width and depth are conceptually 140 x 140 mm, structural acrylic members in 5 mm thickness increments, so members must remain fine and transparent in proportion. Do not add extra storeys or enlarge the enclosure. Some empty transparent space remains to make the composition breathable.

Develop these localized model details:
1. Upper left white room and stair assembly: carefully cut layered white-greyboard door surrounds, recessed door panel, quiet wall panel seams, thin skirting, a short built-in bench, clear stair landings and very fine miniature handrails. Keep the room masses and stairs recognizable and keep the front open for viewing.
2. Bottom center existing sci-fi inclined structure and printed floor rail panel: retain their recognizable main forms and add restrained white and light-grey flat appliqué plates, rib strips, recessed grille strips, inspection panel rims and precise end caps. All visibly realizable as 3D-printed cores with small cut-board surface details. Avoid excessive pipes and industrial clutter.
3. Existing lower pyramid bay: preserve the large white pyramid. Add a small adjacent clear/frosted acrylic display element with delicate etched wave lines and one miniature operating pedestal. This is an abstract physical representation of a VR/hologram station, no floating digital effects.
4. The shallow middle empty central deck: add a compact touch-response demonstration insert at the back, with a white ribbed relief wall forming a gentle wave, a small stepped/pixel relief patch on the floor, and a short partial ceiling strip of suspended white fins on a visible thin carrier. Keep front and most of this bay open. Show tiny red scale figures touching the wall, crouching to the floor, or reaching toward the ceiling element. Every piece is attached to a floor, wall, or overhead support.
5. Right two-bay curved terrace: retain its existing location and basic long low curved form, but enrich it with varying-width layered white-board contours, slight rises and dips, several small tactile cube blocks integrated into the terraces and a couple of small square recesses. Keep the large white cube at the right recognizable. Thin neatly cut board edges and stacked layers are clearly visible, with no giant freeform mountain. Include a seated red miniature and another touching a cube.
6. Top central small occupied deck: add one restrained miniature white workbench with a tiny hand-sculpted object, a small box-frame scanner/3D-printer representation and a short shelf with miniature output objects. Red human figurines work at the bench. The deck must not become cluttered.
7. Keep the low far-left bay mostly open, with a small orientation pedestal and one red miniature.

Materials and appearance: transparent acrylic edges and real light refraction, matte ivory-white dense model card/greyboard with subtle paper texture and visible clean laminated edges, matte white 3D-printed cores with very faint print lines, a few pale-grey detail strips. Tiny monochrome red physical model figures, consistently the same scale as in image 1. Figures must remain clearly plastic scale figures, not realistic people. Preserve the warm accents of the original model, use gentle concealed warm-white floor-edge illumination and only a restrained cool-white glow at the digital/touch station. All electrical effects look like actual miniature LEDs behind frosted material. No magical luminescence or holographic floating objects.

Photography: one coherent landscape-format wide photograph, whole model and grey plinth visible with margins, camera closely matching image 1, crisp focus across the model so small construction details are legible, soft studio ambient light, subtle real shadows, neutral subdued background. Make it convincingly a finely hand-built, achievable physical architectural maquette photographed on a tabletop. No captions, dimension arrows, labels, typography, watermarks, split views, inset closeups or collage. Maintain the recognizable overall model of image 1; change primarily the interior detailing.
